title: Backward value scan lacks single-predecessor check; over-confident value at CFG join
description: StoredValueScanner.java:114. resolveStoredValue only validates the prev->cur fall-through edge, never that cur has a single predecessor, so at a control-flow join it attributes the fall-through path value to the store with full confidence. Failure: LDA #$05 / BEQ t / LDA #$0A / t: STA $8000 returns fullyKnown 0x0A, ignoring A=$05 on the BEQ path. The immediate-fold and AND/ORA-fold paths bypass the engine merge (resolveLoad path is safe as it uses merged inStateAtStore). Fix: require block-leader / single-predecessor before folding a local immediate. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): resolveStoredValue now aborts to unknown() at a control-flow join, detected via isControlFlowJoin (incoming flow Reference to cur from an addr other than prev). RESIDUAL: unresolved computed/indirect jumps leave no reference, so a join reached only by a jump table is not detected -- conservative in the safe direction (worst case a fold we'd otherwise make), not a wrong-value risk.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: recoverCallArgument guesses bank register (A-first), recording wrong bank
description: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:558. recoverCallArgument tries A then X then Y and returns the first that resolves to any immediate, not the register the helper actually reads. Failure: LDX #3 / LDA #$80 / JSR SelectBank (helper takes bank in X, its store not locally resolvable) -> A-first scan returns $80, engine records bank 0x80 instead of 3; downstream refs retargeted to wrong overlay, EOL comment lies. Fix pattern: propagate unknown() when the convention is ambiguous rather than a confident guess. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): recoverCallArgument now scans the register the helper actually stores into its mechanism (HelperModel.argReg from StoredValueScanner.storeRegister on the switch site) instead of the A-first guess. Strictly dominates old behavior: the STX-helper failure now records the correct bank; transform helpers degrade to prior behavior, never worse. RESIDUAL follow-up: a helper that stores a DIFFERENT register than the caller loads (e.g. TXA / STA mechanism) still mis-attributes, needing recursive convention inference inside the helper body. Not filing separately unless it bites.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: Build pipeline: YAML -> .gdt data-type archive generator (Gradle task)
description: Per gib.1.2 review decision (struct source of truth, option 3 from the start): a Gradle build task with Ghidra jars on the classpath walks the descriptor/types YAML and emits a .gdt data-type archive via FileDataTypeManager.createFileArchive(). The loader consumes ONLY the .gdt (standard archive API, no YAML parser in runtime). Rules: .gdt is a build artifact — never committed, never hand-edited, CI always regenerates. Bonus: the .gdt doubles as a standalone publishable artifact usable in stock Ghidra.

title: Design: memory map schema and system descriptor format
description: Design the data model that describes a game system architecture: ROM regions (cart, BIOS), RAM regions, IO port ranges, mirroring rules, initial data type definitions (structs, enums). Goal: one descriptor file per system (YAML or JSON) drives the loader with zero hard-coded system knowledge in Java/Python. Output: draft schema + one worked example (e.g. SNES).
notes:
DESCRIPTOR DATA SOURCES (2026-07-03 survey):
- mist64/c64ref — canonical structured C64 reference (src/kernal/, src/c64io/, src/c64mem/); structured text + Python generator that can be adapted to emit JSON/YAML. THE upstream to consume.
- sajattack/c64-asm-labels — ready-made whole-memory-map label files in ACME/KickAssembler/radare2/VICE-.sym formats. CHECK LICENSE — derived from 'Mapping the Commodore 64' (Leemon), possible encumbrance like c64_ghidra.
- VICE .sym format ('al <hexaddr> .<label>') = de-facto C64 symbol interchange; Ghidra ImportSymbolsScript parses similar.
- KickAssembler built-in MOS6526_CIA/MOS6581_SID/MOS6569_VICII structs = cross-check for IO register offsets.
- c64-wiki Memory_Map banking table — the $0001 LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN combinations to encode as named bank configurations in the descriptor (the part no existing loader handles).
Schema implication: descriptor needs (a) regions, (b) named bank configurations selecting overlay sets, (c) symbol/label imports with provenance, (d) IO register struct definitions.
BANK-SWITCHING DESCRIPTOR DESIGN (user, 2026-07-03): decompose per-game banking info as MECHANISM + INITIAL STATE.
- C64: mechanism = write to $01; initial state = #$37 (BASIC+KERNAL+IO active, CHARROM inactive). Later add cartridge GAME/EXROM lines — note .crt header bytes 0x18/0x19 literally store EXROM/GAME line state, so for cartridges initial state can come from the container, like iNES headers do for NES.
- NES: mechanism = the Mapper (defines memory segmentation + what constitutes register reads/writes); initial state = PCB-specific -> descriptor-friendly.
- Implication for schema: MECHANISM is code-shaped (pluggable strategies — NES mappers will need several categories of register-access handling, e.g. MMC1's serial 5-write loading), INITIAL STATE is pure data. Descriptor names a mechanism + parameters + initial state; the earlier 'named bank configurations' idea becomes the STATE SPACE the mechanism transitions through.
- C64 = deliberately simple POC of the mechanism plumbing (single-register write) before NES stresses programmability.
DRAFT 1 DELIVERED (2026-07-03): ghidra/SCHEMA.md (design notes) + ghidra/descriptors/c64.yaml (worked example; YAML-validated, 8 bank states / 3 windows / 7 fixed regions).
Key schema decisions in draft:
- windows/occupants model: banked ranges declare candidate occupants; states assign occupant per window. Enumerated states table (C64: 8 PLA rows) OR mechanism-computed (NES) — schema allows both.
- context_register field links descriptor to the bundled 6510 language's bank context field (TMode-style); agreement needs a build-time check (open question 3).
- symbol sets are user-toggleable with game-RE defaults (kernal-api ON, kernal-zeropage/basic OFF since games reuse those).
- 'kind: entry' symbols create functions on EMPTY ROM slots so KERNAL calls resolve to named stubs without ROM bytes.
- descriptor states hardware facts (repeat_to mirrors); loader chooses representation.
OPEN QUESTIONS for user review (in SCHEMA.md): (1) struct source of truth: inline YAML vs c64ref-generated vs .gdt archives; (2) symbol interchange: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer, or .sym canonical; (3) descriptor<->language agreement check for context register.
TODO before close: verify ROM SHA1s against real ROM set (placeholders emptied); adapt c64ref generator for the generated/*.yaml sources; VICE cross-check of the 8-state table.
SCHEMA REVISION 1.1 (user input, 2026-07-03): READ/WRITE ASYMMETRY. Bank mapping must differentiate read vs write targets — C64 writes under BASIC/KERNAL ROM always reach the RAM beneath; $D000 varies by state (IO: r/w both chips; CHARGEN: read ROM, write RAM). Modeled as occupant property 'on_write' (not per-state): omitted=self, <occupant>=write-through, 'mechanism'=writes are bank-mechanism events (NES mapper writes — doubles as analyzer watch-list), 'none'=open bus (Ultimax later). Per-state variance falls out of occupant selection automatically.
GIB.2 IMPLICATION recorded in SCHEMA.md: Ghidra resolves references to ONE address space — LDA $A000 and STA $A000 in the same bank state cannot target different blocks. Context-aware resolution hook must be ACCESS-TYPE-AWARE: (context, address, access) -> block. Loader-policy mitigation meanwhile: analyzer annotates stores into ROM-mapped ranges with reference to on_write target.
REVIEW DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03) — SCHEMA.md open questions resolved:
(1) Structs: YAML canonical, .gdt generated at BUILD time FROM THE START (not staged via load-time builder). Loader only consumes .gdt. New bead grm-1.5 (blocks gib.1.3) for the generator + Gradle task. .gdt = build artifact, never committed; CI regenerates.
(2) Symbols: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer (community files, cc65/KickAss output).
(3) Descriptor<->language: LOAD-TIME check — loader verifies language declares banking.context_register, clear error on mismatch.
IMPLICATION flagged to user: building the Gradle/.gdt pipeline is the first real EXTENSION CODE, which per the incubation rule ('extension gets its own repo from creation time') approaches repo-birth.
close_reason: Schema/system-descriptor format validated end-to-end by the grm-1.3 POC: the compiled c64.map + c64.gdt (from machines/c64.yaml) drove a real Ghidra 12.1.2 C64 PRG import — regions, banked windows (home-in-base), IO chip structs, and KERNAL symbols all applied correctly (headless-verified, CHROUT Function@base:ffd2). Schema documented in docs/SCHEMA.md + docs/MAP_FORMAT.md. Residual schema growth (cartridge EXROM/GAME bits, .crt, flow-tracked banking) is tracked under the gib.2 line, not this design bead.

title: Survey Ghidra loader/extension API and existing console loaders
description: Audit: what API surface does Ghidra expose for loaders? What existing open-source console loaders exist (NES, SNES, PS1)? Determine if extension vs. script vs. core loader plugin is the right artifact type. Survey: GhidraNES, ghidra-snes-loader, ghidra-psx-ldr, etc. Output: a short design note on the extension/loader API contract and gaps vs. our needs.
notes:
PRIOR ART SEEDS (from user, 2026-07-03):
- https://github.com/hippietrail/RetroGhidra — multi-retro-system Ghidra extension; POSSIBLE CONTRIBUTION TARGET instead of reinvention; survey must include contribute-vs-build verdict
- https://github.com/c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra — possible useful C64-specific material
- https://cesarmiquel.github.io/tech/art/science/design/2020/03/13/week-13.html — general Ghidra console-RE article, many good links
- HN 46882389 (Ghidra MCP tools) — spun off to bead game-music-extraction-gib.3
IN-TREE FINDINGS (D:/git/ghidra): 6502 + 65C02 languages exist, NO 6510 variant (identical ISA; $00/$01 port is a memory-map annotation concern, not decode). No console loaders in-tree; nearest templates: BinaryLoader, MotorolaHexLoader (opinion package).
RETROGHIDRA SURVEY VERDICT (2026-07-03): BUILD NEW, upstream shallow pieces later as goodwill.
- ~29 loaders, all uniformly SHALLOW: parse header -> createInitializedBlock -> entry point. No loader anywhere models IO registers, full hw memory maps, or banking; zero use of overlay address spaces (even Atari 2600 mirrors are just separately-named blocks).
- C64 support = thin CommodorePrgLoader.java (single CODE block, no C64 labels), C64CrtLoader.java (3 labels), D80 filesystem. No KERNAL labels, no VIC/SID/CIA, no banking.
- Architecture = one Java class per format, knowledge as Java constants; NO data-driven layer (an unused GSON GhidraLabel.java hints it was considered). Our descriptor-driven design would FIGHT their architecture, not extend it.
- Apache 2.0; alive but small (35 stars, ~4-5 contributors, bursty maintenance; Ghidra 12.x compat PR #23 open with engagement but unmerged).
- Use as REFERENCE for Ghidra API boilerplate only. After our C64 loader works, consider upstreaming format-detection pieces as standalone PR.

C64_GHIDRA SURVEY (2026-07-03): c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra has working C64BinLoader.java (PRG load-addr detection, override option, zp/stack blocks, overlay mode) and c64LabelAddrs.py (74KB comprehensive KERNAL/BASIC ROM+RAM symbol tables). NO LICENSE SPECIFIED -> cannot reuse code/data verbatim; either ask author or regenerate labels from primary sources. No banking model, no VIC/SID/CIA annotations.

GHIDRA-MCP (2026-07-03): bethington/ghidra-mcp very active, Apache 2.0, 256 tools; assumes binary already loaded, modern-platform-oriented. Useful AFTER loader works (agent-driven verification of blocks/labels). Recorded on gib.3. HN criticisms: tool-count bloat degrades LLM tool use; fork quality concerns vs LaurieWired original.
BROAD SURVEY (2026-07-03): Three memory-map patterns exist in the wild, all painful:
(1) Overlay blocks at same vaddr (fortenbt/Ghidra-SMB3INES-Loader, Dan Sanderson C64 Crossroads walkthrough) — hardware-truthful but cross-block flow analysis breaks;
(2) Separate non-overlapping blocks per bank (kylewlacy/GhidraNes, 40+ mappers) — no addr conflicts but loses runtime-address correspondence;
(3) Manual annotation after flat load (Sanderson: ~38 hand edits for a small program).
NOBODY does descriptor-driven automation — that is the confirmed gap.
Key references: SMB3 loader = best overlay+symbol-injection example (11,500 symbols); achan1989/ghidra-snes-loader = best LoROM/HiROM mirror modeling (study for SNES phase); zeroKilo/C64LoaderWV (.d64); Dan Sanderson https://dansanderson.com/mega65/crossroads-part-2/ = clearest description of the manual workflow our loader automates; retroreversing.com/ghidra = curated plugin list.
GHIDRA-C64HELPERS CONTENTS (user inspection, 2026-07-03): (a) 6510-specific processor definition — easily incorporated into our extension (extensions can bundle languages; resolves the no-6510-in-tree gap properly instead of aliasing 6502); (b) PETSCII visualizer — feeds the generalized string-detection feature (bead grm-1.4).
close_reason: Survey complete. Deliverable: ghidra/SURVEY.md in GME (migrates with epic). Verdict: build new extension; RetroGhidra as API reference only. Key findings: descriptor-driven automation is a confirmed empty niche; upstream banked-memory space is open with 6 motivating issues and a clear proposal shape (TMode-style context + context-aware address resolution hook); c64ref is the clean descriptor data source; 6510 language bundle-able from ghidra-c64helpers precedent.

title: State-field packing has no cumulative-width validation (>32 bits silently corrupts)
description: MapCompiler.java:604. parseStateFields accepts each field with bits<=31 but never checks the SUM. packState does packed |= fieldValue << shift; shift += bits. Once cumulative shift >= 32, Java shifts are mod-32 so the field wraps into low bits and packed int corrupts. Failure: two 20-bit fields (sum 40) -> second field overwrites first, wrong initial_state/states.value, no error. Fix: reject total width > 32. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed. Added a cumulative-width check in parseStateFields: sum of all banking.state field widths must be <= 31. Refined the bead's '>32' threshold to '>31' via primary-source evidence: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:193 derives the whole-state mask as (1 << stateBitNames.size()) - 1 where stateBitNames has one entry PER BIT, so total==32 gives (1<<32)-1 == 0 (empty mask) in addition to packState's mod-32 shift wrap. Cap at 31 keeps both the packing and the runtime mask correct. Verified: all descriptors+sketches still compile; a sketch with two 20-bit fields (total 40) now fails at build with 'banking.state total width 40 bits exceeds 31'.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: Truncated ROM: vector read past EOF throws uncaught IOException out of load()
description: NesRomLoader.java:345. checkRange validates window offsets against the DECLARED prgSize, never actual file length. A .nes declaring 32KB PRG with a 16KB body passes all gates; the high window block creation fails-and-is-swallowed but is still added to placed; labelVectorTargets then readBytes(fileOffset,2) past EOF -> IOException propagates out of load() (try/finally does not catch it), aborting import with an exception dialog instead of a logged skip. Fix: validate declared PRG against provider length up front, or guard the vector read. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.
notes: Fixed by option (a): validate declared PRG against actual provider length up front, right after InesHeader.parse. If header.prgFileOffset()+header.prgSize() > provider.length(), log 'Truncated iNES image...' and return gracefully. Placed BEFORE any resource allocation (board resolution, gdt open, block creation) so the early return leaks nothing. This is the right-altitude fix: guards the single trusted invariant (declared==actual PRG bytes) once, covering both the swallowed block-creation failures and the previously-unguarded vector read at labelVectorTargets (provider.readBytes past EOF -> IOException out of load() -> exception dialog). No NES headless test harness exists (banktest is C64-only); verified by compile + reasoning.
close_reason: P2 code-review fixes: truncated-ROM up-front guard + cumulative state-width validation. compileJava + buildExtension + buildMap/validateSketches all green; width gate empirically confirmed.

title: MapCompiler accepts maps: keyword offset that the runtime cannot resolve
description: MapCompiler.java:66 (EXPR_KEYWORDS includes offset) vs DescriptorSupport ExprParser.parseFactor (no offset case) and referencedFields (excludes only last/second_last). A descriptor using offset compiles clean but at load time referencedFields returns {offset}, which != the banked field name, so NesRomLoader logs needs exactly one banking.state field and never places the window (or env.get(offset) throws). Valid-looking descriptor -> silently incomplete memory map. Fix: either drop offset from the compiler keyword set or implement it in the runtime. Verdict CONFIRMED.
notes: Fixed by DROPPING offset from the grammar (not implementing it). Rationale: the loader places every computed window as a CONTIGUOUS Ghidra block, so the window-relative CPU offset is added IMPLICITLY by the affine mapping; evalExpr returns one base offset per window/bank with no per-byte term. 'offset' in an expression would double-count (PRG[bank*0x4000+offset]) or be misread as a state field (PRG[offset] -> referencedFields {offset} -> 'unknown state field'). It was also unused by every descriptor. Removed offset from MapCompiler.EXPR_KEYWORDS + its javadoc; synced docs/SCHEMA.md, docs/MAP_FORMAT.md, docs/vision-board-banking.md to state the offset is implicit. Verified: all machines/*.yaml + sketches recompile clean; a sketch using 'offset' now fails at BUILD time ('identifier offset is neither a banking.state field nor one of [second_last, last]') instead of compile-clean/fail-at-load. Runtime (DescriptorSupport.ExprParser) needed no change -- it never claimed offset.
close_reason: Dropped the unimplementable/unused 'offset' keyword; compiler grammar + docs now match the runtime. Build-time rejection verified.

title: M2: NES discrete mappers — UxROM/AxROM/CNROM/GxROM/BNROM via memory-latch strategy
description: First NES banking, per docs/vision-board-banking.md M2. Add the memory-latch strategy: store anywhere in a declared range, written value (or field) is the state, optional bus-conflict rule (effective value = written AND ROM byte at target — some discrete boards). Descriptors for UxROM (16K switchable $8000, fixed-last $C000), AxROM (32K $8000), CNROM (PRG fixed; CHR-only banking — near-trivial PRG side), GxROM/BNROM. Overlay-generation L4 (interim): one overlay per bank on the switchable window only — fixed windows are single blocks; no bank-by-window duplication (contrast GhidraNes MMC1Mapper.java:27-45). ACCEPTANCE: on real UNROM titles (Mega Man, Castlevania, Contra, DuckTales), bank-switch stores are detected, cross-bank JSR/JMP auto-resolve to the correct overlay, unknown-state sites get explicit ambiguity markers. GME payoff: nes/megaman + nes/bionic music-driver RE gets bank-aware disassembly.
close_reason: M2 discrete mappers shipped. memory-latch strategy (range store, shift/mask field extraction, bus-conflict AND when target is constant bank-invariant ROM, write-only-latch load resolution) via shared StoredValueScanner extracted from register-write with zero C64 regression (banktest suite byte-identical, 13/13, re-run on final build). Five shipping descriptors: nes-uxrom(2)/cnrom(3)/axrom(7)/gxrom(66)/bnrom(34); nes.yaml renamed nes-nrom.yaml; build.gradle machine tasks now data-driven glob. Loader realizes switchable computed windows home-in-base + <window>_B<v> overlays and records the board in program info; NesBankingAnalyzer reads it. Engine: computed-window retargeting, residence clamp (execution implies mapping), helper-call propagation (const helper state or call-site immediate arg recovery), and disassembly/function kick at cross-bank flow targets. ACCEPTANCE on real ROMs: Mega Man (UNROM) 153 switch annotations, 1507 cross-bank JSR/JMP refs primary into PRG_LO_B4/B5/B6, 7435 instructions disassembled inside bank overlays (13337 total vs 353 without banking), helper FUN_dc21 unrecoverable-arg site gets explicit WARNING. Castlevania: helper JSR sites detected with honest ambiguity markers (bank arg loaded from memory variable - stage-driven, statically unresolvable). W&W (AxROM): single 32K window, home+B1-B3, vectors from switchable home, 17 switches incl 'bank -> 2 via FUN_ff69'. Contra imports clean but stalls at 717 instrs (indirect-jump dispatch, generic coverage limit). DuckTales absent from ROM collection. Deviation: descriptors carry provisional context_register nesbank (MapCompiler requires it; dormant until grm-bk6). Follow-up filed: grm-5zg (descriptor include mechanism + optional context_register). Unblocks grm-6a7/grm-hsv (M3).

title: M2: extract BoardBankAnalyzer + strategy library (register-write) from C64BankingAnalyzer
description: Split C64BankingAnalyzer into (a) a machine-independent BoardBankAnalyzer engine — CFG worklist dataflow, per-bit partial-knowledge state (migrate PortState toward RegisterValue, which it reimplements), agree-bit merges, call-clobber rules, initial-state defaults, context stamping via ProgramContext.setRegisterValue, switch-site comments/bookmarks — and (b) a strategy library discovered via ClassSearcher, starting with register-write (fixed-address store; masked-RMW backward-scan value recovery already built and verified). Strategy interface owns: candidate-write recognition, value recovery (delegating to shared dataflow), state-field update emission with per-bit confidence. Configuration comes entirely from the schema-v2 descriptor (banking.mechanisms). ACCEPTANCE: C64 banktest/banktest2 headless suites pass unchanged (zero regression) with the C64 path running through the generic engine + register-write strategy. See docs/vision-board-banking.md section 6 (L2).
close_reason: BoardBankAnalyzer engine + strategy library extracted; ZERO REGRESSION proven by the new committed banktest suite (tools/banktest: 13 criteria + golden behavior dumps blessed against the pre-refactor analyzer, byte-identical after). Engine (BoardBankAnalyzer, abstract): CFG worklist dataflow, BankState per-bit value+mask (PortState renamed/promoted; RegisterValue's model on ints — full RegisterValue binding blocked on grm-bk6's context register, documented), agree-bit merges, initial-state defaults, effective-state fallback, switch-site EOL comments w/ known/assumed provenance, WARNING bookmarks only when zero bits known, overlay reference retargeting incl on_write, and ProgramContext.setValue context stamping that engages only when the language declares banking.context_register (dormant until grm-bk6 — stock 6502 has none). Strategies: BankSwitchStrategy ExtensionPoint (data/ExtensionPoint.manifest suffix; ClassSearcher discovery, fresh instance per mechanisms[] entry, configured from params) + RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy owning the verified masked-RMW backward scan. C64BankingAnalyzer is now ~60 lines: loader gate + map path + name (bookmark category preserved via getSimpleName). Documented deviation: WARNING bookmark message TEXT generalized (was register-write-specific prose); location/presence unchanged, dumps unaffected. Suite: tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless. Unblocks grm-4iq (memory-latch tier).

title: M1: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline (nes.yaml)
description: NES entry point per docs/vision-board-banking.md M1: iNES header parsing (mapper number, PRG/CHR sizes, trainer), board-descriptor registry keyed by mapper number with user override as a loader Option (pattern: Loader.getDefaultOptions, Loader.java:176 — board choice rides alongside the language pair, no LoadSpec changes), nes.yaml descriptor in schema v2. NROM end-to-end first: fixed PRG mapping (16K mirrored or 32K), CPU-space MMIO regions with PPU/APU/controller register types+symbols, vectors labeled and disassembled. CHR stays out of CPU space (GhidraNes parks it at $0000 in CPU space — known-wrong precedent, see NesMapper.java:161-203). No banking yet; this proves the loader stack is system-neutral. GME payoff: nes/smb (NROM) becomes the first Ghidra-navigable GME music target.
close_reason: iNES loader + board registry + NROM baseline shipped, verified end-to-end headless vs ghidra 12.1.2. machines/nes.yaml (schema v2): PPU/APU register structs (NESdev-checked), nes-mmio symbol set, vector slots, physical PRG + computed windows PRG[0]/PRG[last] — the last expression handles NROM-128 mirroring AND NROM-256 with zero special-casing. NesRomLoader: iNES header parse (magic/PRG/CHR/mapper/trainer), constant maps:-expression evaluator (ints, last, second_last, arith; state-field exprs deferred to bank engine), NES Board import option; NesBoardRegistry scans bundled machines/*.map for system.board.ines_mappers (data-driven: new boards = new descriptors, no Java). Loader stack proven system-neutral: descriptor interpretation extracted from C64PrgLoader into DescriptorSupport (regions/perms/volatile/subregions/types/symbols), C64 loader delegates, compiles green. VERIFIED: SMB (NROM-256) — correct blocks/perms, MMIO labels, typed vectors, NMI/RESET/IRQ functions, 1066 instructions from canonical reset; Pac-Man (NROM-128) — mirror windows placed, vectors resolve, $FF00 reset disassembled. CHR deliberately not loaded (PPU space deferred per vision §5.4). Follow-up filed for cosmetic ZERO_PAGE/STACK pspec-block conflict messages. Unblocks grm-4iq. GME payoff: nes/smb is now Ghidra-navigable.

title: M1: descriptor schema v2 — state tuples, mechanisms list, physical spaces, computed occupants, mode layouts
description: Generalize the board descriptor schema (SCHEMA.md / machines/c64.yaml) per docs/vision-board-banking.md section 5: (a) banking.state becomes a named tuple of fields mapping onto context-register sub-fields (RegisterValue per-bit partial knowledge); (b) banking.mechanism becomes mechanisms[] list, each a strategy instance with params and the state fields it feeds; (c) physical: spaces backing ROM images laid out once, with windows mapping into them via a deliberately tiny expression language (state fields, integer arithmetic, last/second_last, window-relative offset); (d) mode-dependent layouts[] selected by state fields (MMC1/MMC3 PRG modes). (a) banking.state = named field tuple ({name,bits}, first field = bit 0); (b) banking.mechanisms[] = strategy instances with opaque params + sets validation; (c) top-level physical[] spaces + window maps: 'SPACE[expr]' with compile-time-validated mini-expression language (ints, state fields, last/second_last/offset, + - *, parens); (d) memory.layouts[] mode-dependent window sets keyed by when:{field:value}. Note: maps: values must be quoted inside YAML flow mappings ([ is a flow indicator) — documented in SCHEMA.md; vision doc examples show the unquoted aspirational form.

title: Board-level banking engine: machine-independent four-layer roadmap
description: Umbrella for the design vision recorded in docs/vision-board-banking.md (v1, 2026-07-07): first-class, data-driven board-level banking — four layers (L1 optional CPU-assist register; L2 strategy-driven write detection + value recovery; L3 pure-data interpretation; L4 application via context register + resolution hook, overlays as interim ceiling). Stepping stones: C64 (M0, shipped) -> schema v2 + NES NROM (M1) -> strategy library + discrete mappers (M2) -> MMC1/MMC3 protocol strategies + bank-placement inference (M3) -> MMC5 + GB MBC machine-independence proof (M4) -> core hook integration gated on RFC #9349 signal (M5). Guiding principles in the doc, notably: analysis over interrogation (infer bank placement from flows, never ask upfront — retire the GhidraNes per-bank combo-box pattern) and physical-space backing with windowed views (no bank-by-window block explosion). Related: grm-bk6/grm-wkk (C64 L1/L2 upgrades, parallel track); GME bead gib.2 (upstream engagement).

title: Bundle 6510 sleigh language (PORT register + c64bank context fields)
description:
Bundle a 6510 language variant with the extension (precedent: grue74/ghidra-c64helpers), replacing the fallback_language 6502:LE:16:default used today (c64.yaml cpu.language already names 6510:LE:16:default).

Contents beyond stock 6502:
- PORT register modeling the on-die $00/$01 port; specialized zp constructors (operand==$01, and ==$00 for DDR) route LDA/STA/etc through the register instead of memory — makes bank-switch idioms ordinary register dataflow (see grm-wkk for why).
- c64bank context register with three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (TMode-style; RegisterValue gives per-bit partial knowledge for free).
- Consider undocumented/illegal opcodes while in there (games use them).

Keep decode otherwise identical to stock 6502. Loader stops passing fallback_language once bundled.
notes: 2026-07-07 DESIGN CORRECTION (user): on-die-ness places only the mechanism REGISTER, never banking semantics — the PLA wiring of port bits to LOROM/HIROM/CHAREN is external, C64-board-specific. Counterexample: 6510T in the 1551 drive has the identical port wired to drive-control signals. Therefore the 6510 language must be SYSTEM-NEUTRAL: define PORT as an anonymous 8-bit on-die register routed from $00/$01 accesses; NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN naming, no c64bank truth-table knowledge in the slaspec. Per-system bit naming, if wanted, goes in a per-system pspec variant via register alias (ARM precedent: ARMt.pspec 'TB alias ISAModeSwitch') or stays entirely analyzer/descriptor-side.
close_reason: Bundled 6510 sleigh language shipped. data/languages/6510.{slaspec,ldefs,pspec,cspec} + sleighArgs.txt; build.gradle sleighCompile task (ghidra.pcodeCPort.slgh_compile.SleighCompile, SoftwareModeling/Generic/Utility lib classpath, -a) wired into buildExtension; compiled .sla gitignored (build artifact) + packaged. LANGUAGE: 6502 decode/semantics byte-identical PLUS on-die PORTDDR($00)/PORT($01) registers; specialized zero-page constructors (OP1/OP2, inherited by OP2LD/OP2ST) route DIRECT $00/$01 accesses through the registers so STA $01 -> PORT = A is register dataflow (verified via pcode probe: results=[PORT] inputs=[A]); indexed ($01,X) stays memory. SYSTEM-NEUTRAL per the 2026-07-07 design correction: port named anonymously, NO LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN, NO c64bank context register in the slaspec (bank meaning is board wiring, not CPU arch). Two sleigh gotchas solved+documented: (1) unquoted register-name display token is parsed as an operand ref and breaks export-size inference -> quote it ("PORT"); (2) dynamic *[register] export compiles to a STORE-via-pointer (results empty) not a clean register write -> static export PORT is required and works (coexists with the tables' memory exports like stock OP2:A). LOADER: DescriptorSupport.resolveLanguageId reads system.language, verifies availability, falls back to 6502 only if unavailable; C64PrgLoader uses it; fallback_language removed from c64.yaml (loader stops passing it, per acceptance). ANALYZER kept green without the grm-wkk propagator refactor: register-write mechanism gained optional 'register' param (c64.yaml: register: PORT); StoredValueScanner.writesRegister/readsRegister detect the on-die register via getResultObjects/getInputObjects; strategy ORs address|register so 6510 (register) and the 6502 fallback (address) both work. ZERO REGRESSION: C64 banktest suite 13/13 PASS and both dumps BYTE-IDENTICAL to goldens under the 6510 language; NES Mega Man byte-identical (153 switches/1507 cross-bank refs/13337 instrs) confirming the shared StoredValueScanner change is safe. Clean-from-scratch gradle build green; zip packages the language. Illegal/undocumented opcodes DEFERRED to grm-azg (not a pure win -- defining them makes data bytes decode as instructions, hurting code/data separation; needs an opt-in-variant design decision). context_register kept as c64bank in c64.yaml (MapCompiler still requires the field; making it optional is grm-5zg) but documented as the not-yet-realized application-layer channel; stampContextRegister stays dormant. Unblocks grm-wkk (TMode-style propagator refactor now has its PORT register).

title: TMode-style bank tracking: model 6510 port as CPU register + per-bit context fields
description:
Adopt the ARM Thumb (TMode) tracking pattern for C64 bank state, per the priority rule: use existing Ghidra infrastructure before rolling our own.

How ARM does it (verified in D:/git/ghidra source):
1. Sleigh models the mode as a REAL CPU REGISTER: ISAModeSwitch (TB). Every mode-changing instruction's pcode writes TB (macro SetThumbMode, ARM.sinc:208-211), so mode changes are ordinary register dataflow visible to SymbolicPropogator, the emulator, and the decompiler.
2. TMode is a 1-bit CONTEXT FIELD controlling decode. Static direct branches stamp the target from sleigh itself via globalset (ARMinstructions.sinc:2416 'TMode done by HAddr24's globalset') — no Java involved.
3. ArmAnalyzer (a ConstantPropagationAnalyzer) bridges dynamic flows: reads the propagator-tracked TB value at computed flows (ArmAnalyzer.java:813) and stamps ProgramContext.setValue(tmodeRegister, target, target, value) (ArmAnalyzer.java:825); future disassembly consumes the context.

Mapping to C64 (hardware-truthful: the 6510 port at $00/$01 is ON THE CPU DIE, not external memory):
- Bundled 6510 sleigh adds a PORT register; specialized constructors for zp opcodes with operand==$01 (STA/LDA/etc $01) read/write PORT instead of memory. Then LDA $01 / AND #$F8 / ORA #$05 / STA $01 is pure register dataflow — whole-value tracking suffices whenever the incoming PORT value is known. SymbolicPropogator failed on this idiom only because the port was modeled as memory.
- c64bank context register gets three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (c64.yaml already anticipates 'TMode-style' at banking.context_register). RegisterValue natively supports per-bit partial knowledge (value+mask ctor RegisterValue.java:89; combineValues merge :205-233) — C64BankingAnalyzer's PortState(knownMask,bits) is a reimplementation of it.
- initial_state fallback = ProgramContext DEFAULT value on the context register (pspec / setDefaultValue), replacing the hand-rolled 'assumed from initial' logic.

Scope: blocked on bundling the 6510 language (grm backlog). When it lands, refactor C64BankingAnalyzer toward ConstantPropagationAnalyzer + PORT register tracking; keep the mask-algebra backward scan only as fallback for the stock-6502 fallback_language path, or delete it. Genuinely-partial bases (ORA into unknown PORT) still exceed whole-value tracking — per-bit context fields + defaults cover representation and fallback; evaluate whether the residual gap matters on real code.
notes:
Also refines the gib.2/RFC #9349 claim: 'SymbolicPropogator cannot resolve masked idioms' is true only while the port is modeled as memory. Precise upstream framing: whole-value tracking is sufficient once banking mechanisms are modeled as registers (as ARM does); what's missing in-tree is per-bit partial knowledge of VALUES (RegisterValue covers context/storage, not VarnodeContext propagation).
2026-07-07 abstraction refinement (user-driven): the general stack is 4 layers — (1) mechanism register definition [language, only when architecturally on-die]; (2) mechanism-write detection + value recovery [analyzer, strategy-driven]; (3) interpretation into bank state [descriptor data]; (4) application to decode/refs [context + RFC hook, universal]. What makes tracking cheap is layer-2 STATIC IDENTIFIABILITY of mechanism writes, not on-die-ness (Z80 'OUT (n),A' is equally identifiable with no CPU register). PORT-as-register is a per-CPU layer-2 optimization; layers 2-4 are needed by every banked system. See grm-bk6 note for the system-neutral language requirement.

title: Phase 0 bank-aware analyzer: flow-track bank state, retarget refs into overlay banks
description: The gib.2 Phase 0 interim (RFC docs/rfc-banked-memory.md): a Ghidra analyzer that (a) tracks C64 bank state along control flow from banking.initial_state, updating at determinable writes to the banking mechanism address ($0001, from banking.mechanism in the descriptor — which MapCompiler must now emit into c64.map, currently dropped); (b) for instruction operands targeting a banked window, when the effective occupant for the access differs from the base-space home block, adds an explicit primary reference into that occupant's overlay space (legal today: ReferenceDBManager.addMemoryReference has no same-space constraint). Includes write-under-ROM: WRITE accesses route via the occupant's on_write (STA $A000 with BASIC banked in -> RAM_A000::a000 even in the default state). Data-driven from c64.map; no hardcoded C64 facts beyond schema. Unknown/conflicting state -> leave defaults + bookmark. Demonstrates demand for the upstream RFC and gives correct cross-bank xrefs today.
design: Bank-state tracking: simple forward dataflow over the CFG (worklist; per-block in/out state; merge conflict -> unknown), NOT SymbolicPropogator — transparent and sufficient for the LDA #imm/STA $01 idiom; stored value from immediate-load lookback within the block (A/X/Y). state = value & mechanism.mask; occupants from banking.states. Refs: addMemoryReference(instr, overlayAddr, refType, SourceType.ANALYSIS, opIndex) + setPrimary; skip when effective occupant == home AND access is not a rom write-under. EOL comment or bookmark at bank-switch instructions showing the new state. Gate canAnalyze on executable format == C64 PRG loader name. Extend synthetic test PRG with a state-5 section + state-7 write-under-ROM to verify.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). C64BankingAnalyzer (AbstractAnalyzer, INSTRUCTION_ANALYZER, priority REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), gated on executableFormat == loader name): forward dataflow to fixpoint (known->conflict->UNKNOWN lattice) from entry/function seeds at banking.initial_state; bank switches recognized via WRITE ref to banking.mechanism.address with backward immediate-load scan (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm, block-bounded, clobber-aware); refs into banked windows retargeted to the state occupant's overlay (reads/exec) or its on_write occupant (writes — incl. write-under-ROM in the HOME state), SourceType.ANALYSIS, set primary, default demoted; EOL 'bank -> N (...)' comments; WARNING bookmark on undeterminable switch; idempotent. MapCompiler now emits banking.mechanism (was dropped); MAP_FORMAT.md updated. Verified: LDA $A000@state5 -> RAM_A000::a000 READ primary; STA $E000@state5 -> RAM_E000::e000 WRITE; STA $A000@state7 -> RAM_A000::a000 WRITE (write-under-ROM); JSR $FFD2 untouched. Subagent-found API gotcha: CodeUnit.getScalar(0) returns null for bare immediates — pull Scalar from getOpObjects instead.

title: C64 PRG loader (6502): overlays, IO struct annotation, KERNAL symbols; consume .gdt+.map
description: The grm-1.3 POC loader. Ghidra 12.x AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (class name MUST end 'Loader'): override load(Program, ImporterSettings); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default), gated on .prg extension / valid 2-byte load-addr header. In load(): read 2-byte LE load address, place PRG bytes; read bundled c64.map (gson) + c64.gdt (FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive); create region MemoryBlocks; create per-bank OVERLAY blocks (MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock/createUninitializedBlock isOverlay=true, distinct block name per occupant -> distinct overlay space); apply IO structs from .gdt at subregion addresses (program.getDataTypeManager().resolve + DataUtilities.createData CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA); apply inline symbols (SymbolTable.createLabel IMPORTED + addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL entry stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction); set entry point at load address. Defer 6510 language + c64bank context register + flow-tracked banking (separate bead). Locate bundled resources via Application.findDataFileInAnyModule.
design: MEMORY LAYOUT (corrected per user 2026-07-04 — references must resolve in the BASE space): Do NOT make all window occupants overlays; that reproduces the #6651 dangling-reference bug (JSR $FFD2 resolves in base space, so labels in overlay spaces are never consulted). Instead: the occupant selected by banking.initial_state (C64 state 7 = BASIC/IO/KERNAL) is the HOME block in the BASE (default) space; only the ALTERNATE occupants become overlay spaces. Base space = 7 always-visible regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF) + PRG (initialized, split RAM_MAIN around it) + window HOME blocks: BASIC@$A000 (empty ROM slot R+X), IO@$D000 (apply VIC/SID/CIA .gdt structs + color RAM + IO1/IO2), KERNAL@$E000 (empty ROM slot R+X). Overlays (own spaces, same nominal addr): RAM_A000, RAM_D000, CHARGEN, RAM_E000. CONSEQUENCE: KERNAL symbols (CHROUT@$FFD2 etc.) and IO structs are applied in the BASE space home block, so refs from PRG code resolve NOW without gib.2. Residual (refs INTO alternate/overlay banks) is the gib.2 problem — POC creates overlay blocks + labels but does NOT wire cross-refs into them; a future overlay-aware labelling/analyzer pass (or gib.2) attaches those. Program entry point = PRG load address (base space).
notes: REOPENED for code-review fixes (2026-07-04): (1) RAM regions were read-only (write flag passed as isIo) — centralize r/w/x into canWrite(kind)/canExecute(kind): RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w, applied at all block-creation sites (fixes the ad-hoc drift across createRegionBlock/createRamMainSplit/createWindowOccupant/createIoSubregions). (2) RAM_MAIN split produced two blocks both named RAM_MAIN — give the carved halves distinct address-suffixed names (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader: separate blocks are normal; join() can't merge FileBytes-initialized PRG with uninitialized RAM). (3) drop unused regionsByName param from createRegionBlock/createPrgBlock.
close_reason: Review fixes applied + re-verified headless (Ghidra 12.1.2). #1 RAM now writable (centralized canWrite/canExecute: RAM=r+w+x, ROM=r+x, IO=r+w — consistent across all 4 block-creation sites, base & overlay); #2 split halves distinctly named RAM_MAIN_0800/RAM_MAIN_0807 (aligned w/ stock BinaryLoader; join() can't merge init+uninit); #3 dead regionsByName param removed. Re-smoke confirms all RAM blocks w=true, IO w=true/x=false, ROM w=false/x=true, distinct names, CHROUT Function@ffd2, entry@0801, IO structs applied, Import succeeded.

title: Build-time map compiler: c64.yaml -> c64.map JSON; bundle .gdt+.map into extension data/
description: Runtime loader (grm-1.3.2) needs the C64 memory map without a YAML parser. Add a build-time compiler (MapCompiler, in the existing build-only gdtBuilder source set) that reads machines/c64.yaml and emits a c64.map JSON resource (regions, windows/occupants/subregions, banking states, inline symbols). JSON chosen because Ghidra bundles gson (Framework/Generic/lib/gson-2.13.2.jar) so the runtime loader parses it with ZERO shipped dependency. Also redirect the grm-1.5 .gdt output and the new .map into a bundled data dir (data/machines/) and make buildExtension package them, so both artifacts ship in the extension zip. Both are generated build artifacts: gitignore them, never commit.
design: c64.map JSON schema (contract with grm-1.3.2): { system:{id,name,language}, regions:[{name,start,end,kind,type?,comment?}], windows:[{name,start,end,occupants:[{name,kind,image?,on_write?,subregions?:[{name,start,end?,size?,repeat_to?,kind?,type?,comment?}]}]}], banking:{initial_state,context_register,state_bits,states:[{value,:,...}]}, rom_images:{:{size,occupant}}, symbols:[{set,default(bool),region?,entries:[{addr,name,kind,comment?}]}] }. Addresses as decimal JSON numbers. Compiler emits INLINE symbol entries only (source: sets not yet generated). Passes repeat_to through (loader decides mirror policy). Output data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; buildExtension.dependsOn buildGdt+buildMap (attach lazily). Document the schema in docs/MAP_FORMAT.md.
close_reason: Build-time map compiler complete + verified: gradle buildExtension alone bundles data/machines/c64.gdt + c64.map; c64.map matches frozen schema (7 regions, 3 windows w/ IO subregion types+repeat_to, 8 banking states, kernal-api inline symbols); snakeyaml stays build-only. Commit 872c669.

title: POC: C64 loader that maps banked RAM/ROM, IO ports, and PRG load address
description: Implement a minimal proof-of-concept Ghidra loader for the Commodore 64 that (a) reads a PRG file's 2-byte load-address header and places code correctly, (b) maps the banked memory layout — RAM under KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN, plus the IO region — using Ghidra overlay address spaces to represent the overlapping banks selectable via the $00/$01 processor port, (c) annotates IO chip registers (VIC-II, SID, CIA1, CIA2, color RAM), (d) applies initial struct/label definitions for known hardware registers. Validates that the system descriptor design (gib.1.2) is sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Open question to resolve in design: how faithfully to model banking given Ghidra's static memory model.
notes: DESIGN (2026-07-03, decided w/ user): (1) Descriptor delivery = COMPILE MAP AT BUILD TIME. Build tooling emits c64.gdt (types, existing) PLUS c64.map (regions/windows/banking/symbols) as bundled extension data resources; the runtime loader reads BOTH via non-YAML means (no snakeyaml in shipped extension). (2) POC language = stock 6502:LE:16:default; defer bundling 6510 + c64bank context register + flow-tracked bank state to a later bead (gib.2 track). Banking already decided = overlay address spaces. LOADER API (Ghidra 12.x, source-verified): override load(Program, ImporterSettings) on AbstractProgramWrapperLoader (NOT the classic 6-arg load); findSupportedLoadSpecs returns one LoadSpec w/ LanguageCompilerSpecPair(6502:LE:16:default,default); class name MUST end in 'Loader'. Overlays: MemoryBlockUtils.createInitializedBlock(...,isOverlay=true) once per bank, distinct block name per bank -> distinct overlay space (BASIC_ROM:a000). Bundled .gdt: Application.findDataFileInAnyModule('c64.gdt') -> FileDataTypeManager.openFileArchive(f,false); apply via program.getDataTypeManager().resolve(dt,DEFAULT_HANDLER) + DataUtilities.createData(...,CLEAR_ALL_UNDEFINED_CONFLICT_DATA). Symbols: SymbolTable.createLabel(addr,name,IMPORTED)+addExternalEntryPoint; KERNAL stubs via AbstractProgramLoader.markAsFunction(prog,name,addr). Decomposition: grm-1.3.1 build-time map compiler+bundling; grm-1.3.2 the 6502 PRG loader.
close_reason: POC complete + headless-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2). Both children done: grm-0xt (build-time c64.map compiler + .gdt/.map bundling) and grm-974 (6502 PRG loader). Acceptance (a) PRG 2-byte load-addr header read + code placed, (b) banked layout mapped, (c) IO chip registers annotated (VIC/SID/CIA/color RAM via .gdt structs), (d) struct+label defs applied — ALL verified. DESIGN REFINEMENT vs original description: original said 'use overlay spaces to represent overlapping banks'; we improved to HOME-IN-BASE (occupant selected by initial bank state = home block in BASE space; only ALTERNATES become overlays) because pure-overlay banks reproduce the #6651 dangling-reference bug — base-space code (JSR $FFD2) never consults overlay labels. Result: default bank config fully cross-referenced today (CHROUT Function@base:ffd2), pre-gib.2. Descriptor design (gib.1.2) validated as sufficient to drive real C64 analysis. Residual = refs INTO alternate/overlay banks (gib.2 context-aware resolution).

title: Game System Architecture Loader
description:
Root epic for ghidra-retro-machines: a descriptor-driven Ghidra loader extension that sets up complete retro system architectures — memory maps, banked windows (mechanism + initial state), IO chip register structs, copyright-safe ROM slots, symbol sets — from per-machine YAML descriptors (machines/*.yaml). Initial target: Commodore 64. Design docs: docs/SURVEY.md (founding survey), docs/SCHEMA.md (descriptor schema).

LINEAGE: incubated in CBongo/game-music-extraction as beads epic gib.1 (children gib.1.1-gib.1.5 = grm-1.1-grm-1.5); migrated here at repo-birth 2026-07-03. Related work still tracked in GME: gib.2 (Ghidra core banked-memory upstream proposal), gib.3 (Ghidra MCP tooling).
notes:
ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03):
1. MVP input format: PRG (2-byte load address header).
2. Banking: overlay address spaces for MVP — best Ghidra can do today. IO region always needed by music code; BASIC/KERNAL/CHARGEN rarely needed by music code itself but frequently involved in the LOADER code paths (esp. KERNAL). Long-term: improving Ghidra core banked-memory support is a stated motivation of this whole effort — see bead game-music-extraction-gib.2.
3. ROMs (copyright): symbol-only labels by default (e.g. KERNAL entry points); reserve labeled memory-map slots so users can pull their own ROM dumps in via File > Add To Program; optional loader ROM-path options possible later.
4. Schema: evolving descriptor schema from day one, NOT hardcode-C64-first. Solo development until project is more baked; collaborators later.
5. Build-vs-contribute still open pending RetroGhidra survey (gib.1.1).
REPO NAME DECIDED (user, 2026-07-03): ghidra-retro-machines. Verified collision-free on GitHub (no exact match; no confusable neighbor in the Ghidra/RE space). Pitch: 'give Ghidra the whole machine, not just the file' — descriptor-driven system architecture loaders for retro computers and consoles. Layout affordance: machines/c64.yaml, machines/nes.yaml. Repo-birth trigger reached: gib.1.5 (.gdt build pipeline) is the first extension code; at repo creation, migrate this epic's subtree per the MIGRATION NOTE above and move GME's ghidra/ design docs (SURVEY.md, SCHEMA.md, descriptors/) into the new repo.

title: C64 loader: optionally populate KERNAL/BASIC/CHARGEN ROM regions from user-supplied ROM files
description: Today the c64.yaml ROM regions ($A000-$BFFF BASIC, $E000-$FFFF KERNAL, CHARGEN) are created but NOT populated with bytes (the copyrighted ROMs are not bundled), so ROM code is undisassemblable and ROM-sourced data is unavailable. Add an OPTIONAL path for the user to supply their own ROM dump files at load time, which the loader reads into the corresponding ROM regions as initialized blocks. Mechanism options: Ghidra Loader options (Loader.getDefaultOptions -> user-visible import options carrying file paths), or a post-load script/analyzer that reads paths from a config and Memory.setBytes/createFileBytes into the ROM blocks. Keep it optional: absent ROM files -> current behavior (uninitialized ROM regions), no regression. Benefits: (1) ROM routines (KERNAL/BASIC entry points) become disassemblable and callable-into from user code; (2) ENABLES the ROM-sourced dual-home case in grm-1.7.1 -- the canonical CHRGET->$73 fixture needs the BASIC ROM CHRGET source bytes present so a createByteMappedBlock at $0073 can share them. Until this lands, grm-1.7.1 must start with the PRG-internal copy case (source in the loaded program) rather than CHRGET-from-ROM. Relates to C64PrgLoader / DescriptorSupport region creation and machines/c64.yaml ROM region definitions. Filed at user request during grm-1.7.1 (2026-07-13).

title: grm-1.7.2 tier 2: test emulation-assisted decrypt of a rolling/computed-key loop
description: C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer.apply() already routes a ROLLING/COMPUTED KeyModel (EOR keytab,X etc.) with AUTO confidence to the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness (dirty-watch on the target range, IoPolicy.volatileBlocks) and materializes the read-back bytes via the shared overlay path -- but NO banktest fixture exercises this path, so tier 2 is wired but unverified. Add a rolling-key decrypt .prg fixture (e.g. LDA base,X / EOR keytab,X / STA base,X / DEX / BPL with a JMP into range and a small key table) + a VerifyBankTest branch asserting the emulated recovery produces the correct plaintext overlay and, if the loop reads only initialized RAM, a NOTE (not SUSPECT/WARNING) bookmark. Also cover the SUSPECT path: a loop whose key derives from an IO/uninitialized read should still recover bytes but get a WARNING bookmark (provenance.suspect()). Parent grm-1.7.2 tier 1 is done+tested (commit 2d3815f); this closes the tier-2 verification gap.
close_reason: Tier-2 emulation-assisted decrypt verified end-to-end for BOTH outcomes. Rolling-key happy path (EOR keytab,X, initialized RAM): analyzer routes to grm-edg EmulationRecovery, runs the loop in the p-code emulator during analysis, reads back plaintext 01..08 under dirty-watch, materializes DECRYPTED_2019 with a trusted NOTE. Suspect path (EOR $DC00,X CIA register): emulator answers the hardware read with a policy value, provenance logs an IO read, analyzer recovers bytes (=ciphertext) but downgrades to a WARNING. Deterministic; full banktest suite green in check mode, no existing golden changed. Commits 58d3c03 (rolling), 2aa079b (suspect). (Force-closed: the blocking dep was the parent feature grm-1.7.2 this task verifies; verification is complete.)

title: C64 memory map: let a PRG load at any RAM address, not just RAM_MAIN ($0800-$9FFF)
description: The c64.yaml descriptor's load_target region RAM_MAIN is only $0800-$9FFF, so C64PrgLoader can only carve a PRG into the base address space when its load address falls in that window. A PRG loading elsewhere in real C64 RAM -- e.g. $C000 (the 4K RAM block), or RAM-under-ROM ($A000-$BFFF BASIC, $E000-$FFFF KERNAL) or RAM-under-IO ($D000-$DFFF) -- conflicts with the base block already mapped there and the loader falls back to placing the PRG in a NEW OVERLAY space instead of base RAM. Consequences: (1) the program's bytes are not where a naive base-space consumer expects them; surfaced concretely by grm-edg's EmulationRecovery fixture, whose $C000-loaded PRG landed in an overlay so EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (which copies each block into ITS space) left base $C000 uninitialized -> immediate decode fault. Worked around by loading the fixture at $2000 (inside RAM_MAIN), but that is a fixture band-aid, not a fix. Rethink the C64 RAM modeling so a PRG can load at ANY RAM address: options to weigh -- (a) model all RAM regions ($0000-$9FFF, $C000-$CFFF, and the RAM-under-ROM/IO banks) as load_target-eligible base RAM so createRamMainSplit can carve the PRG wherever it lands; (b) make the loader prefer carving PRG into whichever base RAM region contains the load address rather than only the single load_target region; (c) represent the C64's RAM-vs-ROM/IO banking so RAM-under-ROM loads map correctly. Relates to C64PrgLoader.createRamMainSplit / createPrgBlock and c64.yaml region layout. Discovered during grm-edg (2026-07-12).

title: Partition test suite into chunks with subset selection; full suite gates acceptance
description: Split testing into related chunks runnable independently (candidates: c64-banking, nes-banking, basic+petscii, bit-algebra, plus future per-milestone chunks) so active development runs only the relevant subset fast/often. Mechanism: chunk argument or tag filter on run-banktest.sh (and gradle test tags if the JUnit spike lands), with a documented convention mapping source areas -> chunks. HARD RULE: final acceptance and commits still gate on the FULL suite passing — subset runs are a development-loop optimization only. Consider a 'quick' alias (skip slow analyzeHeadless imports where a cached project suffices) and rough timing measurements to prove the speedup.

title: Testing strategy: golden-image E2E + unit-level framework + suite partitioning
description:
High-level testing strategy for the extension. CURRENT STATE (assessed 2026-07-12, mostly fine for now): end-to-end golden-image regression via tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh check|bless — python generators synthesize test PRGs/ROMs, analyzeHeadless imports with the real loaders, VerifyBankTest.java (~1000 lines) checks criteria and diffs normalized behavior dumps against expected/; build-and-test.sh adds per-worktree isolated extension installs; sibling checkers for petscii and bit algebra. No JUnit anywhere — subagents repeatedly burn time hunting for a framework that does not exist.

THREE QUESTIONS this epic resolves:
(1) UNIT LAYER: would a framework (JUnit via Ghidra's own extension test support — AbstractGenericTest, ProgramBuilder program-fixture classes, gradle test integration) simplify test creation long-term for unit-level testing (MapCompiler parsing, StoredValueScanner bit algebra, strategy dispatch) IN ADDITION TO — not replacing — the E2E golden suite? E2E stays the acceptance authority: it exercises the real loader+analyzer stack headlessly, which unit fixtures cannot.
(2) PARTITIONING/SPEED: split the suite into related chunks (c64-banking / nes-banking / basic+petscii / bit-algebra / per-tool) so that during active development a subset relevant to the current change runs fast and often, while FULL suite passing still gates final acceptance and commits. Needs a selection mechanism (per-chunk driver args or tags) + a documented convention for which chunk covers what.
(3) LEGIBILITY: document the strategy (docs/testing.md + AGENTS.md pointer) so agents and contributors find the harness instead of searching for junit/gradle-test scaffolding that is not there.

Guiding principle: same priority order as everything else — use existing infrastructure first (Ghidra ships JUnit test scaffolding for extensions), mirror how Ghidra's own tree tests analyzers where applicable, roll our own only with recorded justification.

title: SPC700 language sourcing: evaluate SPCdra (license/quality) vs writing our own sleigh
description: Prerequisite for grm-1.7.3 discovered by the grm-1.7.4 survey: stock Ghidra ships NO SPC700 processor module (verified: Ghidra/Processors/ has no SPC700; the bead's 'verify' flag was warranted). Community candidate: SPCdra (github.com/qwertymodo/SPCdra) — SPC700 sleigh + .spc file loader + HW register symbols. The .spc loader angle also delivers the fastest 1.7.3 value: .spc music rips are full 64K sound-RAM snapshots = immediate AKAO driver disassembly target (GME dumpspc.pl lineage).

title: EmulationRecovery harness: bounded PcodeEmulator run + dirty-set capture + descriptor-driven IO policy
description: Shared bounded-emulation core decided by the grm-1.7.4 survey (docs/smc-survey.md par.6): given entry address + stop conditions (breakpoint set / exit-range / dirty-watch / instruction fuel / wall-clock) + IO policy sourced from the board descriptor (IO regions -> readUninitialized + beforeLoad behavior), run the interpreted PcodeEmulator over the current Program image (EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram) and return {dirty address set, recovered bytes, stop reason, provenance log incl. IO-read and uninitialized-RAM warnings}. Callers decide materialization (patch / overlay / byte-mapped block / new Program). Serves grm-1.7.2 tier 2, grm-1.7.3 generic uploader tier, and future banking L4 emulator integration (same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer as vision-board-banking.md par.7.1). NOT JitPcodeEmulator (SMC-unsafe passages).
notes: 2026-07-12 IMPLEMENTED + TESTED. Shipped retromachines.EmulationRecovery + support types (src/main/java/retromachines/): EmulationRecovery (core), StopConditions (fuel/wallclock/exit-range/dirty-watch), StopReason, IoPolicy (interface + volatileBlocks(Program) default deriving IO-ness from descriptor-set block volatility), ProvenanceLog (IO_READ/UNINIT_RAM_READ/WARNING/INFO + suspect()), RecoveryResult (dirty AddressSetView + per-range readback + recoveredBytes(start,len)). Uses interpreted ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator (NOT Jit -- SMC-safe by re-decode). API verified against the actual 12.1.2 install (Emulation-src.zip), NOT the D:/git/ghidra checkout which is 12.2. KEY CORRECTNESS FINDING: the concrete BytesPcodeExecutorStateSpace calls the Address-based dataWritten and the AddressSetView-based readUninitialized (via PcodeEmulationCallbacks.Wrapper injecting thread; null for shared state) -- overriding the other members of each overload pair compiles but silently never fires. Capture is gated by a 'capturing' flag flipped true only after loadProgram+initializeRegisters so setup writes don't pollute the dirty set; register/unique writes filtered by isMemorySpace(). TEST (option b per grm-32f, since JUnit/ProgramBuilder test jars are not shipped in the public install): tools/banktest/mkemutest.py generates a constant-EOR in-place decrypt .prg; VerifyBankTest.java emurecoverytest branch drives the harness and asserts stop=DIRTY_WATCH, recovered=01..08, not suspect, dirty covers target; golden tools/banktest/expected/emurecoverytest.dump (STEPS 39). Full suite green in check mode. NOTE: fixture loads at $2000 (inside RAM_MAIN) because the C64 map only carves PRGs into base space within $0800-$9FFF; a $C000 load lands in an overlay that loadProgram copies to a different space -> filed grm-dvx to let PRGs load at any RAM address. Unblocks grm-1.7.2 tier 2.
close_reason: EmulationRecovery bounded-emulation harness implemented and tested end-to-end. retromachines.EmulationRecovery + StopConditions/StopReason/IoPolicy/ProvenanceLog/RecoveryResult, on interpreted PcodeEmulator (SMC-safe), API verified against the real 12.1.2 install. Dirty-set capture uses the two callback overloads the concrete state actually invokes (Address dataWritten + AddressSetView readUninitialized via the thread-injecting Wrapper), gated post-load. Descriptor-sourced IO policy via block volatility feeds provenance (IO/uninit-RAM reads -> suspect()). Regression: banktest emurecoverytest fixture (constant-EOR decrypt .prg) green in check mode (stop=DIRTY_WATCH, recovered=01..08, not suspect). Follow-up grm-dvx filed for C64 any-address PRG load. Unblocks grm-1.7.2 tier 2 and grm-1.7.3 generic uploader tier.

title: End-user docs: README.md 'what it does / how to use it' guide with known-limitation workarounds
description: README.md today is contributor/roadmap-oriented (vision, board status, milestone notes). title: SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy: override depositHelperArgument (route via tracked select at call-site in-state)
description: Found during grm-6a7.2: a bare data-write-only MMC3 helper (STA $8001 with arg in A) is classified a helper with argReg='A' and the WHOLE select-data mechanism width, and call-site recovery uses depositHelperArgument's DEFAULT (deposit across full width) because SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy does not override it — misrepresenting the call as writing select+prg_mode+r6+r7 at once. Correct behavior mirrors serial-shift's override, but with a twist: the target depends on the TRACKED SELECT at the call site's in-state, not the switch site's address — the override signature receives the switch site but the deposit must dispatch on the caller's in-state select value (check what recoverCallArgument passes; may need the call-site in-state plumbed into depositHelperArgument — evaluate whether the existing signature suffices [switchSite + argValue + stateMask] or needs an inState parameter added with a default-preserving overload). Select known -> deposit only the targeted field (ownedMask = that field); select unknown -> ownedMask = r6|r7 with nothing known (honest poison); CHR select -> ownedMask=0 no-op. Fixture: extend nesmmc3test2 (H's callers already set up the known/unknown select contexts — add criteria on the recovered annotation values).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11 from grm-6a7.2 report item 3. Interacts with grm-6a7.2's requiresOnEntry (a proper override reduces the over-wide effectMask that also feeds modifiedMask). USER ASSESSMENT (2026-07-12): bare data-write-only helpers are probably rare-to-nonexistent in real MMC3 games -- a JSR wrapping a single STA wastes cycles when you're racing the beam, so real helpers almost certainly set select+data together. Still worth implementing for mask-width precision (the over-wide default effectMask pollutes summaries/modifiedMask even for the common two-write helper shape). Treat as precision cleanup, not an expected real-game bug; keep P3.
close_reason: Implemented SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument override with state-routed dispatch. Signature grew a field-local inState param (BankSwitchStrategy interface + default + SerialShift override, which ignores it -- its routing is address-keyed); BoardBankAnalyzer.recoverCallArgument localizes runDataflow's outState into the helper mechanism's field space and passes it down. Override: even switchSite (select-write helper) deposits select+mode fields from the arg byte; odd (data-write helper) dispatches on fieldValueIfFullyKnown(inState, selectField) -- known+tracked routes to that one target field (ownedMask = field alone), known+CHR = verified no-op (ownedMask=0, no comment/no warning), unknown = honest poison of all configured target fields only (never select/prg_mode). Fixture nesmmc3test2 extended with CallerC (CHR no-op) and CallerD (R7 routing); criteria G4-G7 added; G1-G3 unchanged. Golden re-blessed for nesmmc3test2 only: e107 went from the fabricated select=2 to fully-known select=6/r6=2; e128's false select=3 comment gone (wholly-unknown deposit takes warning branch; pre-existing requiresOnEntry warning bookmark stands). RESIDUAL (per-item-6 check): requiresOnEntry/modifiedMask function-summary width is built from each function's own switch sites' effectMask, not CallEffect.ownedMask, so H's own summary stays mechanism-wide -- unaffected by this fix, still the grm-6a7.2 over-approximation. Suite: SUITE OK (check), 12/12, all pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: PETSCII mapping core: data-driven byte->display-string API (unblocks BASIC detokenizer)
description: The subset of grm-1.4 that grm-odt.1 (BASIC detokenizing analyzer) needs — scoped deliberately to unblock it without the NES/SNES tile-table half or Ghidra Charset registration (those stay on the parent). Deliverables per the design inputs recorded on grm-1.4: (1) a Java-callable PETSCII byte->display-string API (e.g. PetsciiMapper), usable outside Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery, for programmatic comment-text building; (2) both charset variants (unshifted/graphics and shifted/lowercase) selectable per call; (3) a STABLE escaped rendering convention for control/graphics bytes ({CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}-style — pick, document, freeze: it lands in golden dumps); (4) mapping data lives in a DATA file (machines/generated/ or data/, following basic-tokens.yaml / c64ref precedent), not hardcoded Java, and is shaped so future Ghidra Charset registration (parent bead) reads the same source; (5) screen codes explicitly OUT of scope here (separate mapping, parent bead). Include a small unit-test-style verification (builder-adjacent or a tiny JUnit if the repo has test infra — check; if none, a verify main() like GdtBuilder's pattern). API should be reachable from analyzer code (src/main/java/retromachines/).
design: BRIEF (scouted 2026-07-11; petcat escape tables archived at scratchpad/petscii-escapes.md). ESCAPE CONVENTION: adopt VICE petcat's SHORT ctrl1[]/ctrl2[] bracket names verbatim ({wht},{down},{rvon},{clr},{F1}..{F8},...) for $00-$1F/$80-$9F, and petcat's {$xx} lowercase-hex fallback for EVERYTHING else non-printable — including the $A0-$FF graphics range (do NOT invent names; do NOT use petcat's cbmkeys[] key-combo names — input-oriented, not glyph-oriented).
