title: SMC: survey — Ghidra Debugger/p-code emulator leverage for self-modifying code recovery
description: Research bead, feeds all three use-case children: what can Ghidra's Debugger-era machinery (PcodeEmulator, TraceRmi, emulation scripts, 'Emulate' UI) do for us headlessly and programmatically in 12.1+? Questions: (1) can we run a bounded p-code emulation of a copy/decrypt loop over program bytes WITHOUT a live target (pure emulator, no gdb/frida), capture resulting memory, and write it back into the static Program (or a Trace snapshot converted to Program view)? (2) what are the fuel/termination controls (max instructions, memory faults on unmapped IO reads — retro code touches IO registers constantly; need a fault policy: zero-fill vs abort)? (3) is Trace/snapshot the right persistence for 'memory image after boot-init ran', navigable alongside the static view? (4) precedents: existing Ghidra scripts/plugins doing emulation-assisted unpacking (search ghidra repo + community, e.g. malware-unpacking workflows — same problem shape as C64 decrypt-on-the-fly). Deliverable: written findings on the epic + go/no-go per use case (static vs emulated vs manual).
notes: Filed 2026-07-11. Do this survey FIRST when epic work starts — it decides the approach split for all three children.
close_reason: Survey complete: docs/smc-survey.md. Verdicts: 1.7.1 static (byte-mapped blocks), 1.7.2 emulation-assisted pilot on PcodeEmulator, 1.7.3 static-first (.spc + IPL parse; SPC700 sleigh NOT in stock Ghidra). Debugger = manual tier (GUI Copy Into Program); TraceRmi retro connector no-go for now; VICE snapshot import = cheap high-leverage alternative.

title: SMC: SNES SPC700 upload — cross-processor code extraction to a separate Program
description: Use case 3: SNES games upload SPC700 sound-driver code/data through the APU IO ports ($2140-$2143 handshake protocol) into the sound processor's OWN 64K address space and run it there. Different processor (SPC700 vs 65816), different address space — Ghidra Programs are single-language, so the right deliverable is arguably a SEPARATE Program: recognize/parse the upload (boot-ROM IPL handshake protocol blocks: address+length+data records, well documented on fullsnes/nesdev-adjacent references), extract the transferred image, and materialize a new SPC700-language Program in the project (headless: Program creation API; GUI: an action/script), cross-linked to the source Program (bookmarks/comments at the upload site naming the generated Program and vice versa). STRONG GME TIE-IN: this is exactly the AKAO SNES sound-driver code (FF2/FF3/CT dumpspc.pl lineage in game-music-extraction) — the extracted Program is the disassembly target for the music-driver reverse engineering that motivates the whole toolchain. Design questions: one Program per upload session vs per unique image (games re-upload variants); IPL protocol variants vs game-specific upload loops (AKAO games use their own uploader after boot); where the 'separate Program' convention gets documented for other cross-CPU cases (C64 1541 drive code upload is the same shape!).
notes: 2026-07-12 (user direction) DELIVERABLE SHAPE CORRECTION: output is a SINGLE SPC700 Program (one 64K sound-RAM image) alongside the SNES ROM (65816) Program — NOT one Program per uploaded image. A typical game runs the IPL MULTIPLE times to load separate portions of the SAME SPC700 RAM (e.g. one IPL load transfers the SPC700 driver code, another static instrument/sample data, another filter/echo settings). Recovery model = accumulate ALL IPL transfers into the one SPC700 RAM image at their target addresses (same shape as a fully-populated .spc snapshot). Each ROM-side upload site gets a bookmark cross-linking to the target range it populated. One-language-per-Program still puts SPC700 in its own Program (separate from 65816 ROM), but exactly ONE per game, built from N uploads. Updated docs/smc-survey.md par.5 (grm-1.7.3 Deliverable shape bullet) to match.

title: SMC: run-from-elsewhere — ROM->RAM copy recognition and dual-home code mapping
description: Use case 1: code copied from ROM to RAM and executed there (NES games copy hot loops/NMI stubs to RAM; C64 BASIC copies CHRGET to zero page $73 for speed; C64 games copy loaders under ROM shadows). The 'easy' one-to-one case: recognize the copy loop (source range, dest range, length — the same StoredValueScanner/idiom machinery the banking strategies use can find LDA abs,X/STA abs,X bounds), then materialize the destination as an initialized block populated with the source bytes, with provenance comments and cross-space references bridging call sites to the RAM copy (and ideally back-references to the ROM master). Design questions: loader-time (descriptor hints: 'this region is copied to X at boot' as DATA, e.g. CHRGET) vs analyzer-time (detect copy loops generically); relocation/patching during copy = NOT one-to-one — detect and warn rather than mis-map; interaction with banking overlays (source may live in a banked window). Start with descriptor-hinted static case (CHRGET as the canonical fixture), generalize to detected copies after.
notes: 2026-07-13 IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN DONE (design gate; sonnet subagent research + design note docs/smc-runfromelsewhere-design.md). MECHANIC: Memory.createByteMappedBlock 1:1 overload (Memory.java:397) does LIVE pass-through to the source region = true dual-home (shared bytes), only shows real bytes if source is INITIALIZED. New to the repo. ROM PREREQUISITE (decisive): C64 BASIC/KERNAL ROMs are uninitialized today (c64.yaml rom_images/image keys documented at SCHEMA.md:80 but consumed by NO Java; C64PrgLoader.createWindowOccupant always createUninitializedBlock). So a byte-mapped CHRGET block 0073->BASIC E3A2 shows ?? until real ROM bytes load -> filed grm-mbm (optional user ROM files -> initialized ROM blocks). SCHEMA: a copied_from list on the destination region (name/start/end/source/source_addr), resolving source like the existing on_write occupant names. TWO TIERS sharing one materialization (byte-mapped dual-home + provenance + disassembly, mirroring C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer): Tier A descriptor-hinted CHRGET (needs grm-mbm for real bytes; best-effort block possible before), Tier B analyzer-detected copy loops (LDA src,X / STA dst,X / DEX / BPL, no transform; src!=dst distinguishes copy from in-place decrypt) -- Tier B is TESTABLE NOW with a PRG-internal copy fixture (source initialized), NO ROM dependency. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING: grm-mbm first to unblock Tier-A CHRGET (ROM loading is broadly useful), OR Tier-B first (immediately testable). CHRGET constants (0073-008A / E3A2) are folklore -- verify vs a real BASIC ROM before baking in. NEXT: pick sequencing (grm-mbm-first vs Tier-B-first) and implement.

title: Self-modifying code strategies: run-from-elsewhere, decrypt-on-the-fly, cross-processor code upload
description: Umbrella for making the extension useful on the self-modifying-code patterns retro software actually uses — an axis Ghidra has traditionally handled poorly (static listing assumes bytes at an address are THE code). Three concrete use-case families (children), plus a cross-cutting question: the Ghidra Debugger's emulator/trace machinery may be leverageable for all of them (execute the copier/decryptor in the p-code emulator, capture the resulting memory image, feed it back into static analysis) — traditionally SMC was hopeless statically, but Debugger-assisted 'run it, then analyze what it produced' changes the economics. Design tension to resolve early: which patterns deserve STATIC modeling (descriptor-driven, like banking) vs EMULATION-ASSISTED recovery vs manual workflow documentation. Relationship to banking engine (grm-5tl): banking changes which pre-existing bytes are visible; SMC creates NEW bytes at analysis time — different problem, but the overlay/alternate-view plumbing and the analyzer-pass architecture are shared infrastructure.
notes: 2026-07-12 grm-1.7.4 survey COMPLETE — design tension RESOLVED, full findings in docs/smc-survey.md. Machinery: EmulatorHelper is @Deprecated(since 12.1, forRemoval=true); all emulation work targets ghidra.pcode.emu.PcodeEmulator + PcodeEmulationCallbacks (readUninitialized = IO fault policy hook, dataWritten = exact dirty-set capture) + EmulatorUtilities.loadProgram (plain-emulator harness, no Trace needed). Interpreted emulator is SMC-safe by construction (SleighInstructionDecoder re-decodes each instruction from live state; avoid JIT emulator for SMC). In-tree precedent: EmuX86DeobfuscateExampleScript. DEBUGGER (per user direction, evaluated first-class): pure-emulation mode + GUI Copy Into Program = the manual/interactive tier (document in grm-fy0); headless Trace round-trip buys nothing over direct Memory.setBytes; TraceRmi retro connector (VICE/Mesen) does not exist and stays NO-GO until demonstrated need — VICE .vsf snapshot import is the cheap 80% (real-hardware-fidelity memory image, zero protocol work). Approach split: 1.7.1 STATIC now; 1.7.2 emulation pilot; 1.7.3 static-first with SPC700 language sourcing as new prerequisite (stock Ghidra has NO SPC700 sleigh — SPCdra is the community candidate). Shared EmulationRecovery harness bead created; reuses the same PcodeEmulationCallbacks layer the banking vision picked for L4 (§7.1) — one callback stack serves both features.

title: CBM BASIC program support: token data, detokenizing analyzer, dialects 2/4/7
description: Umbrella for making Ghidra genuinely understand tokenized CBM BASIC programs across the dialect family: BASIC 2 (C64/VIC-20), BASIC 4 (PET), BASIC 7 (C128). Pillars: (1) dialect-layered token DATA shipped as .gdt enums (shared $80-$CB base = single transcription; per-dialect extension lists fork above $CB with conflicting values; BASIC 7 adds $CE/$FE two-byte prefixed tokens -> per-prefix enums); (2) a line-walking detokenizing ANALYZER (line-link/line-number structure, token typing outside quoted/REM contexts, detokenized line comments, SYS-entry detection replacing the loader's wrong entry-function-at-load-address wart); (3) DIALECT parameterization — which enum(s)/walker rules apply comes from the machine descriptor, so PET/C128 support = data + descriptor, not new Java; (4) PETSCII rendering (grm-1.4's C64 half) as the string-literal/REM display layer inside detokenized comments. The BASIC analyzer is a primary design-driving CONSUMER of grm-1.4: it needs a Java-callable byte->display-string PETSCII mapping (shifted/unshifted), not just Ghidra charset registration for string search.
notes: Promoted from grm-odt.1 to an epic at user request 2026-07-11 ('promote the basic analyser to its own epic and flip any dependencies that make sense'). grm-odt (token enum foundation, in flight) and grm-odt.1 (analyzer) re-parented here. Cross-cutting dep: analyzer depends on grm-1.4 for PETSCII; grm-1.4's design must take the detokenizer's requirements as input (recorded on grm-1.4).

title: C64: BASIC line-walking analyzer — detokenized comments, token typing, SYS entry fix
description: Phase 2 of grm-odt (scouted 2026-07-11): new C64BasicAnalyzer extends AbstractAnalyzer (NOT BoardBankAnalyzer — that base is banking-flow specific), gated on C64PrgLoader.NAME + program entry == the descriptor load_target region start (derive 'is BASIC-start PRG' from c64.yaml, do NOT hardcode $0801). Walk classic line structure from load address: 2-byte next-line link, 2-byte line number, tokenized bytes to $00 terminator; program ends at $0000 link. Per line: apply BASIC_V2_TOKEN (phase-1 enum, looked up from the .gdt by name and enumerated into a value->name map — no parallel Java token table, single source of truth) to token bytes OUTSIDE quoted strings; type link+linenum words; EOL/pre comment with the detokenized line text. GOTCHAS from scouting: quote-tracking state machine (PETSCII control/graphics bytes >= $80 inside quotes are NOT tokens); REM lines store the REM token then RAW untokenized text to EOL (must not token-decode); embedded control chars. ALSO FIX pre-existing loader wart: C64PrgLoader marks a function at the raw load address even for BASIC PRGs (line-link bytes, not code) — suppress for BASIC-start PRGs and instead parse a SYS <addr> line if present, marking THAT as the real ML entry (scope SYS parsing explicitly: simple decimal literal only). TEST: tools/banktest-pattern fixture — hand-tokenized 3-4 line .prg (FOR/PRINT/NEXT/SYS 2064) via mkbasictest.py, VerifyBasicTest checks token annotation, line structure, comment text, $0000 terminator, SYS entry; golden dump.
notes: Split from grm-odt 2026-07-11 per scout plan. Depends on phase-1 enum landing (consumes BASIC_V2_TOKEN from the .gdt). Est 1-2 days; medium risk (quote/REM state machine). DIALECT NOTE (2026-07-11): the analyzer must be dialect-parameterized from the start — which token enum(s) it consumes should come from the machine descriptor (c64.yaml -> BASIC_V2_TOKEN; future pet.yaml -> BASIC_V4_TOKEN, c128 -> BASIC_V7_TOKEN + two-byte prefix handling), not hardcoded. BASIC 7 two-byte tokens will need the walker to consume prefix+byte pairs — design the token-lookup interface around (bytes consumed, name) rather than byte->name.
close_reason: C64BasicAnalyzer shipped: line-link walker (shared C64BasicWalker, also used by the loader's BASIC-start sniff), petcat-compatible detokenized PRE comments via PetsciiMapper, link/linenum typed as words, token bytes left undefined (comment carries meaning). Tokens consumed from the .gdt archive DTM (BasicV2TokenLookup; dialect-agnostic (bytesConsumed,name) interface, BASIC-7-prefix-ready). Loader wart fixed: BASIC-start PRGs no longer get a function at the load address; the analyzer marks the SYS <decimal> target instead. TWO CORRECTIONS vs the brief: (1) DATA text IS tokenized in real BASIC 2 (the DATA GOTO gotcha) — no DATA protection branch, verified against petcat/ROM behavior; (2) naive BASIC-start detection false-positived on pure-ML fixtures (stray $00 made one bogus line) — caught by the suite, fixed by requiring the FIRST line to parse cleanly. c64basictest = 11th fixture (B1-B5: exact line renders incl. {clr}/{$a0}/{lgrn}, REM not decoded, SYS entry at 0x842, no function at 0x801); 10 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. Deferred to grm-1.6.1: dialect lists, two-byte prefixes, SYS expressions, variant override (documented in docs/basic-analyzer.md).

title: MMC1: nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring + end-to-end fixture
description: Design B/C-Tier-1 on parent grm-hsv: machines/nes-mmc1.yaml (ines_mappers:[1]; serial-shift mechanism with multi-field targets; layouts keyed off prg_mode: modes 2/3 = fix-first/fix-last 16K windows, modes 0/1 = single PRG32 window — confirm 32K window shape needs no third window-shape concept). Loader materializes (layout x bank) cross product (128K titles = 8 banks; ~2x8 real overlays). Tier 1 placement = normal two-level tracked-state lookup, NO upfront per-bank options (retires GhidraNes BankAddressOption by construction). End-to-end Metroid-shaped fixture (reset dance then never touch Control again -> prg_mode=3 known nearly everywhere).
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 4). Gated on the serial-shift/findIdioms bead. HANDOFF from grm-hsv.1 (2026-07-11): (1) 32K modes (prg_mode 0/1) need PRG[(prg_bank>>1)*0x8000] — evalExpr supports only literals/last/second_last/+-*; add shift-or-divide grammar (+ MapCompiler validation) OR a derived field aliasing prg_bank bits 1-4; do NOT ship modes 0/1 as PRG[0] on the real board (real games use 32K modes). (2) FF1 trampoline (JSR SwapPRG_L -> JMP SwapPRG): calledHelper resolves via getFlows() and does NOT follow one level of JMP — trampoline call sites lose argument recovery unless added. (3) Metroid mailbox commit values resolve unknown -> honest WARNING at MMCWriteReg3; helper-call-argument recovery (LDA #imm/JSR SwapPRG pattern) should still resolve Zelda-style sites — verify HelperModel handles a helper whose write-5 is the switch site (argReg='A'). (4) Keep initial_state prg_mode=3 (reset-dance convention, all surveyed games). (5) Loop matcher is trip-5 only — extend to 4+pre-STA only if a real title needs it. (6) Synthetic serialtest board is mapper 222 (unassigned range); real board = ines_mappers:[1].
close_reason: Real MMC1 board shipped end-to-end. machines/nes-mmc1.yaml (ines_mappers:[1]): all four prg_mode layouts byte-accurate — evalExpr gained >> (right-shift, *-precedence, left-assoc; MapCompiler validator mirrored; baseline diff proved all 9 existing maps byte-identical) so 32K modes map PRG[(prg_bank>>1)*0x8000]. Modes 0/1 identical-window-sets handled correctly by existing runtime (separate per-mode lookups; verbose but correct). Metroid-shaped fixture (LDA #imm/JSR SwitchBank helper idiom, CHR chain no-poison, mode 3->2 transition engineered via byte-identity: prg_bank=7 makes mode-2 switchable WC000 map the same PRG[last] bytes the fixed window had). EXPOSED+FIXED latent engine bug: recoverCallArgument positioned helper args with the mechanism-wide (effectMask,lsb) — wrong for multi-target mechanisms. Fix: BankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument default method returning HelperDeposit(ownedMask, value) — ownedMask distinguishes touched-unresolved (poison) from untouched (preserve); default reproduces historical behavior byte-for-byte; serial-shift override decodes target from switch site and deposits through its field list; ownedMask=0 = verified no-op (CHR helpers can't poison). HelperModel carries strategy+switchSite; helper-call comments render from mechanism-window stateAfter (no more spurious '?'). nesmmc1test = 10th fixture, M1-M10 PASS; 9 pre-existing goldens byte-identical. Real-ROM acceptance gate (Metroid/Zelda/FF1, manual, CI-excluded) now unblocked — FF1 trampoline arg-recovery still a known gap (on bead notes).

title: MMC1: findIdioms hook + serial-shift strategy + fixtures
description: Design A + B on parent grm-hsv. (1) New optional BankSwitchStrategy hook findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty; BoardBankAnalyzer runs it per function like findHelpers and folds matches into the switchResults-shaped map (containment property: merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation unchanged). PROTOTYPE THE HOOK SHAPE FIRST — if it doesn't fold into switchResults it ripples back. (2) SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy: bit-7-set write anywhere $8000-$FFFF = reset (prg_mode->3 known, ORs control with $0C); fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR chain walked statically (writes 1-4 null, write 5 full BankState; target from write-5 addr bits 14:13, value reassembled); canonical STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop via findIdioms (sole loop-body write to range + shift of same reg + trip-count 5 or 4+preloop; seed from ONE backward scan of pre-loop load; commit on loop EXIT edge). Params: multi-field-per-target deposit — targets {0:{fields:[{mirroring,shift 0,bits 2},{prg_mode,shift 2,bits 2}]}, 3:{fields:[{prg_bank,shift 0,bits 5}]}} — strategy-opaque, no compiler change. Source loop matcher shapes from REAL commercial MMC1 disassemblies (Metroid/Zelda), not wiki-invented. Fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable (WARNING), CHR-write recognized-but-discarded. Bit-7 partially-known must NOT silently assume reset (explicit fixture).
notes:
Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11 (design sub-bead 3; sub-bead 2 mode-register-class skipped — MMC1 needs none per Design B, MMC3's is co-emitted in select-data).

REAL-GAME IDIOM SURVEY (2026-07-11, scratchpad/mmc1-idioms.md; Zelda1/FF1/Metroid disassemblies verified mapper 1): (1) ALL THREE games use the FULLY UNROLLED 5xSTA/4xLSR chain — NONE use the counted STA/LSR/DEY/BNE loop the design treated as canonical. PRIORITY INVERSION: the static unrolled-chain walker is the PRIMARY pattern (covers all surveyed titles); the findIdioms loop matcher is SECONDARY (keep — synthetic fixture + unsurveyed titles — but do not gate acceptance on it). (2) FF1 writes to NON-CANONICAL addresses inside each register's 8K window ($9FFF/$BFFF/$DFFF/$FFF9) — design's 'target from write-5 addr bits 14:13' already handles this; make the fixture cover a non-canonical address. (3) Zelda's reset = ORA #$FF then STA to ALL FOUR register addresses (four consecutive reset writes — each is an independent bit-7 reset, must not confuse the chain walker). (4) FF1 reaches the unrolled helper through a JMP trampoline (JSR SwapPRG_L -> JMP SwapPRG) — check findHelpers/Ghidra thunk handling follows it. (5) Value provenance: Zelda = immediates (easy); FF1 = value computed via ROL/AND/ORA well before the JSR (backward scan may fail -> honest WARNING); Metroid = DEFERRED mailbox (call sites write a pending var; a per-frame dispatcher does the real writes with AND/ORA-composed value -> unresolvable -> WARNING, expected degrade; the dispatcher itself is the switch site, call sites are not). A pure peephole matcher misses real call sites in 2 of 3 games — acceptance expectations for hsv.2 should reflect that (fixed windows + reset-dance prg_mode=3 still give most of the value).
close_reason: SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy landed with ZERO engine changes — the planned findIdioms hook proved unnecessary: runDataflow probes computeSwitch on every instruction, so the strategy claims the counted loop's closing BNE as the switch site and the commit flows through the existing switchResults fold (strictly better containment than the hook). Primary recognizer = survey-informed unrolled 5xSTA/LSR bidirectional chain walk (breaks on non-chain instr, control-flow join into any link, X/Y store, RMW); write-5 target from ITS OWN addr bits 14:13 (FF1 $FFF9 non-canonical fixture-proven); quad-resets classified independently before chain logic. Key empirical fix: StoredValueScanner treats shifts as opaque, so preceded-by-LSR-A stores get bit 7 known-clear STRUCTURALLY. Loop matcher: trip-5 STA/LSR/DEX|DEY/BNE, poison suppression by delegating body-membership to the same branch matcher (recognizers cannot disagree). Synthetic board nes-serialtest.yaml on mapper 222 (101 is NOT safe — NESdev duplicate-assignment, not reserved); 4-value prg_mode layouts; 32K modes mapped PRG[0] pending evalExpr shift/divide (grm-hsv.2 flag). nesserialtest = 9th fixture, 16 criteria incl. honest WARNING paths (table seed, partial bit-7 not misread as reset). SUITE OK, 8 pre-existing goldens byte-identical.

title: MMC3: select-data strategy (select+prg_mode co-emission, even/odd-over-range), fixture
description: Design A + Design B resolution (a) on parent grm-6a7: new SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy. Even-address store in $8000-$9FFE range = bank select: resolve byte via existing scanner, deposit bits 0-2 into 'select' field AND bit 6 into 'prg_mode' (co-emission from the same recovered byte; keeps first-match-wins engine loop unchanged). Odd-address store = data: if inState select fully known and targeted field tracked (6->r6, 7->r7) overwrite only that field; select unknown -> poison r6 AND r7; select known 0-5 (CHR) -> leave r6/r7 UNTOUCHED (per-frame CHR swaps must not poison PRG — THE easy-to-get-wrong case, fixture it); data unrecoverable with known select -> only targeted field unknown. Recognizer is (addr&1) over the WHOLE $8000-$9FFF range (sketch's fixed select_address/data_address params are wrong vs hardware mirroring — fix machines/sketches/nes-mmc3.yaml and promote to machines/nes-mmc3.yaml, ines_mappers:[4]). Fixture: synthesized mapper-4 ROM in mknesbanktest.py (immediate select/data pairs, cross-bank JSR through r6-switched window, CHR-select-no-poison case, mode-1 swap); goldens; existing 7 fixtures byte-identical. Note grm-ezl sets[] contiguity: order state fields so this mechanism's fields pack contiguously.
notes: Materialized from parent design 2026-07-11. Parent grm-6a7 design sub-beads 2+3 folded together per design.

title: Release-build strategy on GitHub (Actions matrix across supported Ghidra versions)
description: Set up automated release builds for ghidra-retro-machines on GitHub. Reference sketch = kylewlacy/GhidraNes (.github/workflows/): a reusable _build.yml (on: workflow_call) building with a matrix of ~19 Ghidra versions (10.3 through 12.1) via the antoniovazquezblanco/setup-ghidra@v2.1.0 action (installs Ghidra + exports GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var), temurin Java 21, gradle -PGHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=..., then renames dist/*.zip to ghidra_<ver>_<sha>_<date>_<name>.zip and uploads as artifacts; release.yml triggers on tag push v*, calls _build, downloads merged artifacts, and creates a DRAFT release with gh release create --generate-notes + gh release upload; ci.yml reuses the same _build on ordinary pushes. Adaptations needed for GRM: (1) our build.gradle checks the GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR env var FIRST, which is exactly what setup-ghidra sets — so CI works naturally, no -P needed; (2) matrix should start narrow (12.1.x we actually support) and grow deliberately — sleigh compile + GDT JavaExec tasks may not be version-portable as far back as GhidraNes goes; (3) consider running tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh (analyzeHeadless, works on ubuntu) as a CI quality gate before release assets are published. TRIGGER MECHANISM IS OPEN: user finds tag pushing clunky as a downstream fork — evaluate alternatives: workflow_dispatch with a version input (workflow tags + drafts the release itself, one button in the UI), 'release: published' trigger (draft the release in the UI first, action builds+attaches assets), or push-to-release-branch. Pick whichever makes cutting a release a single low-ceremony step.
design: TRIGGER DECIDED (user, 2026-07-12): workflow_dispatch to start. release.yml takes a version input (e.g. '0.3.0'), runs the _build matrix, then tags and creates the DRAFT release itself (gh release create --generate-notes + upload assets) -- one button in the Actions UI, no local tag push. Tag creation happens IN the workflow from the dispatched ref, so the fork's local clone never needs to push tags. Keep the trigger swappable: structure release.yml so switching to 'release: published' later is just changing the on: block + reading the version from the release tag instead of the input. ci.yml on ordinary pushes reuses the same workflow_call _build.
notes:
Requested by user 2026-07-11. GhidraNes workflow files fetched and verified 2026-07-11 (repo kylewlacy/GhidraNes, default branch main). setup-ghidra action needs auth_token: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN to avoid API rate limits when downloading Ghidra releases.

VERSION-SUPPORT POLICY (user, 2026-07-11): Ghidra will install/keep using an extension built against a different version — it does NOT proactively check compatibility, so a mismatched build may work or break depending on API drift. For the extensions we care about (mostly loaders), the biggest breakage so far is the 11->12 breaking change to the Loader load() method signature. HARD FLOOR = Ghidra 12.0: we will NOT support the <=11 load() API — working around it is a pain (see how GhidraNes contorts to span both). So the matrix may be a small subset, possibly even one build serving several versions. PROCEDURE: check back-support starting at 12.0 and work FORWARD, running the banktest suite against each release to find the true minimum version that works (compat = suite passes, not just compiles). If we find critical dependencies on behavior introduced post-12.0 (candidates to check: ImporterSettings record shape, CommentType enum, SleighCompile invocation, MemoryBlockUtils signatures), DISCUSS each with the user before deciding to work around it vs. raising the floor — do not silently add compat shims.

title: Reconstruct testing procedure for safe parallelization (isolated trees/Ghidra infra, efficient rebuilds)
description: Today the build/test loop is serialized through shared mutable infrastructure, which makes parallel subagent work (now the standing preference) risky: (1) the built extension is installed by delete+unzip into the single per-user Extensions dir (%APPDATA%/ghidra/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC/Extensions/) — two agents installing different builds clobber each other, and an open Ghidra GUI locks the jar; (2) tools/banktest/run-banktest.sh uses shared work/project dirs under one tree; (3) a single working tree means concurrent code edits collide. Rework so N agents can build+test independently: git worktrees (or EnterWorktree) per agent; per-agent Ghidra 'installation' or at least per-agent extension install + headless project dirs — investigate whether analyzeHeadless can point at an alternate extensions dir (e.g. ghidra.user.settings.dir / -vmargs user-dir override) so one shared read-only Ghidra install serves many isolated setting dirs, which is far cheaper than duplicating the 1GB+ install; per-agent scratch/work dirs keyed by worktree. Constraint: keep the rebuild loop reasonably fast — full gradle buildExtension per iteration is already the dominant cost, so prefer solutions that share gradle caches across worktrees and avoid re-unzipping more than needed. Deliverable: updated run-banktest.sh / helper script(s) + documented procedure agents can follow without stepping on each other.
notes: Requested by user 2026-07-11. Motivated by the new user-level 'use subagents whenever it makes sense' policy — current single-install test flow is the main thing forcing serialization. Remember headless gotcha: project path must contain no dot-prefixed path element.
close_reason: Landed: tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh (one-command build -> per-worktree isolated extension install under build/ghidra-home via -Dapplication.settingsdir/-Dapplication.cachedir + GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS -> suite), run-banktest.sh BANKTEST_SETTINGS_BASE hook, CLAUDE.md Build & Test procedure. Verified: main-tree SUITE OK, stamp-skip on second run, isolated settings dir demonstrably used (pass/fail tracked isolated zip while shared %APPDATA% copy present), two worktrees ran concurrently both SUITE OK. Bonus fixes the worktree smoke test flushed out: settings.gradle pins rootProject.name (worktree dir name broke loader discovery via jar name); build.gradle buildExtension now depends on buildPetsciiMap (fresh checkouts shipped a zip missing data/petscii.map -> silently broken C64 BASIC detokenizer; was masked by stale artifact in main tree).

title: C64 BASIC tokens as a Ghidra enum (or similar data type)
description: Idea parked for later: represent the C64 BASIC V2 token set ($80 END ... $CB GO, plus the two-byte extensions if we ever cover BASIC 7/other dialects) as a data type the extension ships — most likely an enum in the generated .gdt (via the YAML types: mechanism / headless GDT builder), so tokenized BASIC program text in a PRG/disk image can be annotated readably in the listing. Open questions: plain enum vs. a typedef'd byte with an analyzer that walks BASIC line links (line-link/line-number/token-stream structure) and comments/detokenizes; where it hooks in (C64PrgLoader for BASIC-start PRGs?); whether symbols/types in machines/c64.yaml is the right home. No urgency — capture only.
design: PLAN (scouted 2026-07-11, read-only exploration). PHASE 1 = THIS BEAD: (1) GdtBuilder (tools/gdtbuilder/src/main/java/gdtbuilder/GdtBuilder.java) supports only kind: struct|flags; add third kind 'enum' — new branch in buildTypes() + buildEnum() mirroring buildFlags() but reading values: [{value,name,comment}] with EnumDataType(name,size) + add(name,value,comment); no bit-shift logic; topo-sort/archive plumbing untouched. (2) machines/c64.yaml types: add BASIC_V2_TOKEN, kind: enum, size: 1 — 76 contiguous tokens $80 END .. $CB GO, hand-transcribed with provenance comment (C64 Programmer's Reference Guide / c64-wiki token table; same 'inline seed' pattern as the KERNAL symbols). No gaps, no 2-byte extensions in stock V2 (BASIC 7 dialects out of scope). (3) docs/SCHEMA.md: document enum kind alongside flags (bitmask vs sequential distinction); check MAP_FORMAT.md types: section. VERIFY: buildC64Gdt + builder's verifyArchive() output shows BASIC_V2_TOKEN with 76 members; spot-check 0x80=END, 0xCB=GO. Rendering mechanics already proven: R6510_PORT_BITS (flags enum) renders symbolically via applyStructType/DataUtilities.createData. NOTE pre-existing loader wart found during scouting: C64PrgLoader marks a function at the raw load address even for BASIC-start PRGs ($0801 = line-link bytes, not code) — fix belongs to phase 2, not here. PHASE 2 = separate follow-on bead (C64BasicAnalyzer line-walker).
notes: Requested by user 2026-07-11. Scoped 2026-07-11 to phase 1 (enum only); phase 2 analyzer = grm-odt.1. DIALECT EVOLUTION REQUIREMENT (user, 2026-07-11, mid-implementation): eventual support for CBM BASIC 2, 4, AND 7 — craft BASIC 2 support so the evolution is natural, maximizing shared data/code. Dialect model: $80-$CB base (76 tokens END..GO) is IDENTICAL across 2/3.5/4/7 = the shared single source of truth; ABOVE $CB dialects FORK with conflicting value assignments (BASIC 4: $CC+ = disk keywords CONCAT/DOPEN/DLOAD/...; BASIC 3.5/7: same values = RGR/RCLR/...) so data model = shared base list + per-dialect extension lists with explicit values, NOT linear inheritance; BASIC 7 adds TWO-BYTE tokens ($CE/$FE prefix + second byte) — not implemented now, but data-file shape must accommodate (per-prefix lists building as separate per-prefix enums, since a 1-byte Ghidra enum can't hold them). Implementation shape: token data in a SHARED data file (following GdtBuilder struct source: precedent), composed by the enum kind; acceptance = adding BASIC 4 later is one extension list + one types: entry in a future pet.yaml, zero re-transcription. Enum names dialect-qualified (BASIC_V2_TOKEN / _V4_ / _V7_).
close_reason: Phase-1 delivered with the dialect-evolution design baked in: GdtBuilder gains a third types: kind 'enum' (explicit value: required — token tables start at 0x80; duplicate names/values rejected since EnumDataType would silently alias; verifyArchive now prints enum member counts). Token data lives in shared machines/generated/basic-tokens.yaml (top-level lists: map; basic2-base = 76 entries $80 END..$CB GO, canonical order independently verified value-by-value) composed via source:+lists: on the types: entry — adding BASIC 4/7 later = one sibling list + one types: entry in pet/c128.yaml, zero re-transcription (grm-1.6.1). Member names keep EXACT BASIC keywords incl. punctuation (INPUT#, TAB(, +, STR$ — Ghidra enum member names empirically unrestricted); YAML 1.1 gotcha found+fixed: bare ON parses as boolean, quoted, documented in SCHEMA.md. buildC64Gdt verify shows BASIC_V2_TOKEN (enum, 76 members); suite SUITE OK all 8 fixtures, goldens byte-identical. Follow-on: grm-odt.1 analyzer (blocked on grm-1.4 PETSCII).

title: runDataflow strategy dispatch: per-call memoization via cacheable() on BankSwitchStrategy
description: Claim 2 of grm-5tl.13 (full design on parent). runDataflow (:426-433) runs every strategy's computeSwitch per dequeue. Research proved MemoryLatch.computeSwitch is fully state-independent (its resolveLoad hook ignores inStateAtStore; resolveStoredValue only forwards that param to the hook) while RegisterWrite's is state-dependent (hook returns inStateAtStore) — so memoize per-address matched-strategy for both, cached RESULT only for cacheable ones. Map<Address,MatchInfo> LOCAL to each runDataflow call (phase 1/2 separation guarantees no mid-fixpoint code changes; discard per call). Add default cacheable()=false to BankSwitchStrategy, MemoryLatch overrides true. Pure memoization — banktest must stay byte-identical. Marginal alone; bundle with grm-5tl.13.1.
notes:
Implemented: added default boolean cacheable() = false to BankSwitchStrategy with javadoc explaining the contract (true iff computeSwitch's result is independent of inState). MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy overrides it to true (resolveLoad only ever resolves loads to a bank-invariant ROM byte, a program-only property; StoredValueScanner's own immediate-value folding is also state-independent). RegisterWriteBankSwitchStrategy left at the false default (its hook returns inStateAtStore).

runDataflow now keeps a local Map<Address,MatchInfo> matchCache (scoped to the call, not a field -- phase 1/2 separation means no instruction appears mid-fixpoint so per-call scoping avoids staleness). MatchInfo(strategy, result): strategy==null records that no strategy's instruction-level predicate matched this address at all; strategy!=null with result==null records a matched-but-non-cacheable strategy (must be re-probed each dequeue); result!=null records a matched cacheable strategy's state-independent value (reused directly, no recompute).

Soundness invariant established by reading both shipped strategies: both gate computeSwitch on an instruction-only boolean predicate (MemoryLatch.writesInRange, RegisterWrite.writesMechanism) and, critically, StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue NEVER returns null -- every path either combine()s to a possibly-unknown-but-non-null BankState or returns BankState.unknown() directly. So for both strategies, 'computeSwitch returns non-null' is exactly the instruction-only predicate, independent of inState -- confirmed RegisterWrite.computeSwitch returns unknown() (not null) when writesMechanism(instr) is true but the store register can't be identified, and otherwise always delegates to resolveStoredValue which is non-null. This means caching 'which strategy matched' per address (not just cacheable results) is sound today: on a cache hit for a non-cacheable match, only that one strategy is re-probed with the current in-state (skipping the other strategies entirely), and if that probe ever unexpectedly returns null (a future strategy violating the state-independent-predicate assumption), the code conservatively treats that dequeue as no-match rather than silently mis-caching -- documented as the safety fallback in the runDataflow comment. A genuinely state-dependent match/no-match strategy would need to override this design (not just cacheable()); none exists today.

title: banktest RMW-split fixture for READ_WRITE reference retargeting (grm-5tl.9)
description: grm-5tl.9 split READ_WRITE references across write-under-ROM boundaries (write->onWrite occupant primary, read->read occupant). Add a fixture: e.g. INC $A000 in C64 state 7 (BASIC read / RAM_A000 write-under-ROM) and assert a WRITE overlay ref to RAM_A000 plus the read resolving to base BASIC (not misdirected solely to RAM_A000, the pre-fix bug). Note the home/base interaction is subtle (when the read occupant is the home occupant the read stays as the base ref), so design the discriminating assertion carefully.
notes:
Added banktest4 fixture exercising the READ_WRITE reference-split path in BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences.

Fixture (tools/banktest/mkbanktest.py, BANKTEST4): LDA #$37 / STA $01 (bank -> 7, the C64 default: LOROM home occupant = BASIC) / INC $A000 (EE 00 A0, a read-modify-write across the write-under-ROM boundary: read occupant BASIC is home so stays on the base ref; write occupant RAM_A000 via BASIC.on_write is non-home so gets a WRITE overlay ref) / RTS.

Three assertions, all discriminating against the pre-fix single-overlay-ref-to-write-target bug:
  D1: primary WRITE overlay ref RAM_A000::a000 exists at 0805.
  D2: no READ overlay ref exists at 0805 (pre-fix, the whole RMW -- including the read -- was misdirected to RAM_A000 as a single ref; this would show up as a READ ref here too, or the WRITE ref's type would encode both).
  D3: exactly 1 overlay ref total at 0805 (rules out an accidental extra ref).
Dump format was NOT changed -- the existing dump (REF ... <space> <RefType> primary=<bool>) already includes RefType, so it was already discriminating; no re-blessing of banktest/banktest2/banktest3 goldens was needed (confirmed via git diff: empty, only banktest4.dump added as new file).

Pre-fix-would-fail argument: pre-fix retargetReferences emitted a single overlay ref per instruction keyed off writeTarget only (no read/write split), so for INC $A000 in state 7 it would add ONE overlay ref to RAM_A000 with the ref's isRead()/isWrite() flags coming from the original READ_WRITE RefType, i.e. still isRead()==true. That ref is what D2 checks for and fails on (readOverlay would be non-null, pointing to RAM_A000 rather than nothing/base). Also D3's count would still be 1 by coincidence in this single-ref case, but D2 alone is the discriminating criterion: pre-fix the read is misdirected to RAM_A000 instead of correctly resolving to base-space BASIC.

title: Banking analyzer efficiency: avoid whole-program re-analysis + memoize strategy dispatch
description: BoardBankAnalyzer: (1) the AddressSetView set param is never used; every added() re-seeds from all entry points/functions and re-runs the full fixpoint, and phase-2 side effects trigger framework re-runs -> up to O(N x wholeProgram). Cache phase-1 output across re-runs or gate on whether set changed reachable state. (2) computeSwitch runs every strategy on every worklist dequeue; the writesInRange/writesMechanism predicate is instruction-only (state-independent) -> compute the mechanism-write candidate set once; memory-latch computeSwitch is fully state-independent and memoizable per address. (3) MemoryLatch.bankInvariantRomByte linear-scans all memory blocks per call (O(banks)); build an overlay-covered interval index at configure(). Correctness-sensitive; needs care + banktest verification. Deferred from /simplify.
design:
REFINED DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to ddbaf5f). All three claims verified against current code. Split into three child beads (this bead becomes the tracker); recommended landing order: claim 3 -> claim 2 -> claim 1. No perf baseline exists — banktest fixtures are 20-90 byte correctness fixtures; all three costs are theoretical at current sizes and become real only on 32KB-512KB images with many re-run rounds.

CLAIM 3 (child a) — bankInvariantRomByte overlay index. STRONGEST STANDALONE.
Current: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte (:145-163) linear-scans all blocks per call (:150-156); called <=~3x per latch-write dequeue (resolveLoad hook :89-97 within MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN=16, plus busConflict branch :113-121).
Design: at configure(), build an AddressSet overlayCoveredRanges = union of base-space shadows of every overlay block (blocks are loader-placed before analyzers run and phase 2 never adds blocks — snapshot stays valid for analyzer lifetime). bankInvariantRomByte becomes block-checks + overlayCoveredRanges.contains(addr) (O(log n)). Effort small; risk very low; identical semantics. Verify: unit test old-vs-new across synthetic overlay layouts (bitalgebra-style differential), plus banktest byte-identity.

CLAIM 2 (child b) — strategy dispatch memoization. CHEAP, MARGINAL ALONE — bundle with claim 3.
Current: runDataflow loop :426-433 runs every strategy's computeSwitch per worklist.poll (:418). Verified: writesInRange (:128-137) and writesMechanism (:71-74) are instruction-only. KEY REFINEMENT: MemoryLatch computeSwitch (:100-126) is PROVABLY state-independent — its resolveLoad hook ignores inStateAtStore, and StoredValueScanner.resolveStoredValue uses inStateAtStore ONLY to forward to hooks.resolveLoad (:171). RegisterWrite computeSwitch (:96-106) DOES return inStateAtStore from its hook — state-dependent, NOT memoizable per address.
Design: (1) Map<Address, MatchInfo> switchCache LOCAL to each runDataflow call (never a field — discard per call, zero staleness; phase 1/2 separation means no code appears mid-fixpoint, worklist never sees newly disassembled addresses). MatchInfo = {matchedStrategy, cachedResult-if-cacheable}. (2) default boolean cacheable() {return false;} on BankSwitchStrategy; MemoryLatch overrides true. (3) On dequeue: cacheable hit -> reuse result; non-cacheable hit -> invoke only the known-matched strategy (skips other predicates); miss -> existing loop, populate. Note mergeAndEnqueue (:458-473) only re-enqueues on state change, so dequeues per address are bounded by lattice height — payoff is a small constant factor. Risk low: pure memoization, banktest must be byte-identical.

CLAIM 1 (child c) — redundant whole-program re-runs. CORRECTNESS-SENSITIVE; GATED ON A FIXTURE.
Current: added() (:144-336) never reads set; runDataflow (:391-456) seeds from ALL entry points + ALL functions (:401-409); phase 1 runs twice when helpers found (:284, :290); phase 2's addOverlayRef fires DisassembleCommand (:812) / CreateFunctionCmd (:816) -> AutoAnalysisManager re-invokes added() with the delta set -> full reseed+fixpoint again. Up to O(rounds x wholeProgram).
CRITICAL INSIGHT: the reseed-everything behavior is LOAD-BEARING — it is how bank state reaches newly disassembled overlay functions (their callers are outside the delta set). "Only process set" is WRONG; a one-shot guard is WRONG (would silently under-annotate cross-bank calls discovered after round 1). Correct scope: skip the ENTIRE re-run iff nothing relevant changed.
Design (fingerprint-gated all-or-nothing skip): static WeakHashMap<Program, Long> keyed by Program identity; fingerprint = functionCount + numInstructions (O(1) reads; safe over-approximation — this analyzer only changes those via its own phase-2 side effects). At top of added() (after mapPath/banking gates): fingerprint match -> log + return true. Write back the fingerprint AFTER phase 2 (so its own side effects force the next round to run). Never cache/diff-merge phase-1 output — annotateBankSwitch (:625-665) never overwrites existing bank-> comments (:658-664), so a stale partial merge would worsen an existing (orthogonal, pre-existing) staleness quirk; all-or-nothing recompute avoids it entirely.
HARD PREREQUISITE before landing: a fixture engineered to require >=2 disassembly rounds (e.g. overlay-bank JSR chain 3+ banks deep) asserting the deepest bank still resolves under skip logic, or a log-based assertion counting full-work runs — current fixtures converge in ~1 round and can't prove the skip doesn't fire early. Document the fingerprint's coverage assumptions at the cache field (future context_register-reading changes could invalidate it silently).

VERIFY (all): GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR=D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC gradle compileJava; banktest run-banktest.sh check byte-identical. Claim 3 also wants a NES/memory-latch fixture (shipped fixtures are C64/register-write — ties into grm-5tl.17).

Note: shipped banktest fixtures are all C64/register-write, so .13.1 would ideally get a memory-latch (NES) fixture — ties into grm-5tl.17.

title: Collapse per-bit loops in StoredValueScanner to bit-parallel algebra
description: StoredValueScanner.java:188-233. combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() are per-bit for-loops that are pure bit algebra. fullyDeterminedByAccumulator == ((~aAcc | oAcc) & mask) == mask (one line). combine == knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()); bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.bits())). Deferred from /simplify because the derivation wants a unit-test pass to confirm (bit-priority oAcc>aAcc-clear>base must be preserved). Add a focused unit test first, then collapse. Quality-only, no behavior change intended.
notes: Done. Collapsed combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() to bit-parallel one-liners, gated by a new exhaustive equivalence check (tools/bitalgebra/BitAlgebraEquivalence.java + 'gradle verifyBitAlgebra', a new no-dep bitAlgebraCheck source set). The check CAUGHT A BUG in the bead's proposed derivation: 'bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & baseBits))' omits the & baseKnown gate, so it sets result bits in UNKNOWN positions (known=0), diverging from the loop and breaking BankState.equals() (which findHelpers' const-merge relies on). Correct form: bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.knownMask() & base.bits())) & 0xFF. knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()) & 0xFF. fullyDetermined = ((~aAcc|oAcc)&mask)&0xFF == mask&0xFF. Proof is complete (bitwise-independent -> 256 enumerated per-bit cases) + 20M-case fuzz. Behavior also still guarded end-to-end by VerifyBankTest banktest2 C1/C2/C4/C6.

title: iNES parse ignores NES 2.0 and is vulnerable to DiskDude flags7 corruption
description: NesRomLoader.java:103. mapper = (h[7]&0xF0) | ((h[6]&0xFF)>>4) unconditionally merges flags7 high nibble; prgBanks = h[4]&0xFF ignores NES 2.0 size/mapper extension. NES 2.0 signaled by (h[7]&0x0C)==0x08, never checked. Failure: (a) a mapper-0 ROM with classic DiskDude! corruption in bytes 7-15 has h[7] high nibble 0x40 -> read as mapper 0x40, wrong/absent board; (b) NES 2.0 image with mapper>=256 or PRG>4MB truncated. Fix: detect NES 2.0 header and honor/ignore flags7 accordingly. Verdict PLAUSIBLE.

title: 6510 language: undocumented/illegal NMOS opcodes (opt-in variant)
description: grm-bk6 bundled the 6510 language but deliberately left out the NMOS undocumented/illegal opcodes (LAX/SAX/DCP/ISC/SLO/RLA/SRE/RRA/ANC/ALR/ARR/SBX, the undocumented NOP/SKB/SKW forms, and the unstable AHX/SHX/SHY/TAS/LAS/ANE). Games (incl. C64 music/demo drivers) do use the stable ones. NOT a pure win: Ghidra's stock 6502 omits them precisely because defining them makes previously-invalid bytes in DATA regions (tables, sample data) decode as instructions, so speculative disassembly can march through data instead of stopping — hurting code/data separation on exactly the data-heavy drivers we care about. So the design question is inline-vs-opt-in: prefer a separate ldefs variant (e.g. 6510:LE:16:illegal, or a pspec/cspec variant) or an analyzer option so users opt in, keeping the default 6510 clean. Model the stable illegals with correct pcode; model or omit the unstable ones with a comment. Verify: (a) compiles; (b) banktest suite still byte-identical (valid decode unchanged); (c) targeted test that a few illegal opcodes decode with sane pcode. Reference: masswerk 6502 illegal opcodes; MAME m6510/m6502 dtables at /z/git/mame.

Also revisit: MapCompiler unconditionally requires banking.context_register whenever banking: is present, forcing the NES boards to declare a provisional 'nesbank' register no language declares yet — make it optional or tie the requirement to the bundled-language milestone (grm-bk6).

title: M3: MMC3 — select-data + mode-register strategies, mode-swapped windows
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: select-data strategy ($8000 even selects target state field R0-R7, $8001 odd writes it — model R6/R7 PRG fields; CHR fields deferred with PPU space) + mode-register ($8000 bit 6 swaps which of $8000/$C000 is switchable vs second-last-fixed). 8K banks: overlay-interim L4 hits ~64 overlays on one window per layout — measure and record the pain as evidence for the M5 core hook (RFC #9349). Function-level bank-state requirements + call-graph propagation land here (large MMC3 libraries need it). Acceptance targets: SMB3, Crystalis, Kirby's Adventure.
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to current engine post grm-5tl.12 refactor). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-hsv flagged.

HEADLINE ENGINE GAP: memory.layouts[] is SCHEMA-COMPLETE BUT ENGINE-ABSENT. MapCompiler validates and emits layouts (cross-validating when: keys against banking.state), but NOTHING consumes them: BoardModel.parse reads only top-level windows[]; NesRomLoader.load reads only windows[] and hardcodes "bank field = first state field". nes-mmc3.yaml declares windows: [] with everything in layouts: — today's loader would create ZERO PRG blocks. Layout consumption is the shared prerequisite for BOTH MMC3 and MMC1 (grm-hsv says verbatim "mode-dependent layouts from schema v2") — file ONCE as a shared bead.

STATE BUDGET: prg_mode(1) + R6(6) + R7(6) = 13 bits of the 31-bit cap — no pressure. Real ceiling found instead: StoredValueScanner.combine masks & 0xFF (single 6502 register scale). Strategies must resolve the stored byte at <=8-bit scale locally then shift into board-state position (both existing strategies do this); passing a 13-bit board mask into resolveStoredValue would silently truncate — implementation pitfall, not schema limit.

MMC3 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: $8000-$9FFE EVEN = bank select (bits 0-2 target R0-R7; bit 6 PRG mode; bit 7 CHR — defer); $8001-$9FFF ODD = data to selected register. Mode 0: $8000=R6, $A000=R7, $C000=second-last fixed, $E000=last fixed. Mode 1: $8000<->$C000 swap. 8K granularity. MIRRORING: any even/odd address in the whole range works — the sketch's select_address:0x8000/data_address:0x8001 params are WRONG vs hardware; recognizer must be (addr & 1) over the range. Fix the sketch in sub-bead 2.

DESIGN A — select-data strategy (SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy):
- computeSwitch(program, instr, inState) ALREADY receives inState — no interface change needed for state-dependent dispatch.
- select = a genuine 3-bit tracked field of banking.state, written by even-address stores via existing resolveStoredValue machinery (bits 0-2). Odd-address store: if inState's select fully known and in targets {6:R6, 7:R7} -> recover byte, overwrite ONLY that field's bits (computeSwitch returns the whole new state, not a delta — merge inState's other fields back in, like MemoryLatch does).
- POISON POLICY (refined from bead text): select UNKNOWN -> R6 AND R7 both unknown (either could be written). Select KNOWN but 0-5 (CHR, untracked) -> leave R6/R7 UNTOUCHED — this case is per-frame-frequent in real code (CHR animation swaps); blanket poisoning would destroy PRG state constantly. Data byte unrecoverable with known select -> only the targeted field goes unknown. Test this CHR case explicitly.
- Table-driven loops (LDA table,X) resolve unknown at local scan — but those are the CHR idiom; PRG switches (only 2 registers) are typically direct immediate pairs, which the backward scan handles natively. Helper rescue is sub-bead 4/6 territory.

DESIGN B — mode register + layouts:
- CONFLICT: runDataflow's strategy loop is FIRST-MATCH-WINS (break on first non-null), but a $8000 write must update both select (bits 0-2) and prg_mode (bit 6). Resolution (a): select-data strategy co-emits the mode bit from the same recovered byte (params gain mode_bit -> prg_mode mapping) — narrowest fix, no engine change. Alternative (b) engine merges multiple strategies' field updates — bigger, defer until a board actually needs independent composition; record the limitation.
- Loader: layouts-only boards need per-layout window realization with MODE-QUALIFIED overlay names (same address range, different modes = unrelated content: e.g. W8000_M0_B<v>). Home block = layout matching initial_state's mode + that mode's home bank. Analyzer: ComputedWindowModel keyed by (mode value, window) not name alone; clampToResidence/retargetReferences look up the active layout from the effective state's mode field first.
- YAML: sketch's layouts:/when:{prg_mode:0|1} shape is already right; the gap is 100% runtime consumption.

DESIGN C — overlay scale + RFC evidence: RFC #9349 = OUR OWN posted ghidra GitHub Discussion (docs/rfc-banked-memory.md is source of record; cites upstream #6651/#5913/#7052/#2546/#1332). Measurement: MMC3 fixture at SMB3 scale (512K = 64 banks; 2 switchable windows x 64 banks, POSSIBLY x2 modes if placement differs per mode -> ~256 overlays worst case, confirm empirically). Metrics: block/space count, wall-clock import+analysis vs UxROM baseline, refsAdded, qualitative UI navigability. Record in docs (vision doc M3 section or docs/mmc3-overlay-scale.md), mirror into Discussion #9349.

DESIGN D — function-level bank-state (Phase 1.5): per-function FunctionBankSummary(requiresOnEntry, effectOnExit); effectOnExit = read-off of Phase-1 outStates at RTS/RTI merged; requiresOnEntry = backward property over call graph (bottom-up over SCCs; lattice already monotone/finite so terminates). Existing findHelpers/HelperModel is the single-write special case — NOTE: MMC3 select+data helpers store TWICE, so HelperModel's argReg reconciliation nulls out and current helper propagation degrades for MMC3 (expected temporary precision gap until this lands). M3 SCOPE: requires-bits derivation + violation WARNING bookmarks ONLY (read-only annotation); NO back-propagation/narrowing of Phase-1 state (mutual fixpoint, termination risk) — that's M4+.

SUB-BEADS (proposed):
1. layouts-runtime [SHARED with grm-hsv, blocks both; HIGH risk] — loader + analyzer consume layouts[]; mode-qualified overlay naming; synthetic 2-mode banktest fixture (two memory-latch fields + layouts, decoupled from select-data).
2. select-data-strategy [MEDIUM] — Design A + mode-bit co-emission (B resolution a) + sketch mirroring fix; cheap fixture (LDA #6/STA $8000/LDA #n/STA $8001/JSR); unit-testable standalone, end-to-end gated on 1.
3. mode-register-strategy — fold into 2 (co-resident on same address; Design B ties them).
4. function-summary-propagation [HIGH risk] — Design D, after 2; fixture: two-write helper called from consistent + violating contexts, WARNING only on violator.
5. overlay-scale-measurement [LOW risk, LAST] — Design C, needs 1+2 landed and acceptance titles loading.
6. (optional) select-data-idiom-hardening — two-write helper support in findHelpers if 2 reviews large; coordinate with 4.

RISKS: first-match-wins composition (above); layouts-only loader path completely unexercised today; mode-qualified naming may double overlay counts; HelperModel degradation between beads 2 and 4 (expected, document); CHR-select non-poisoning is THE easy-to-get-wrong case.
notes: Design attached 2026-07-10 (research: layouts schema-complete/engine-absent -> grm-5tl.18 shared prerequisite; $8000 write must co-emit select+prg_mode from one store — resolve inside select-data strategy, first-match-wins engine loop unchanged; poison policy: known-CHR select must NOT poison PRG fields (per-frame CHR swaps); sketch's fixed select/data addresses are wrong vs hardware mirroring — fix to even/odd-over-range in the strategy bead; RFC #9349 is our own posted Discussion, overlay-scale measurement feeds it). Proposed sub-bead split in design; materialize as children when work starts.

title: M3: MMC1 — serial-shift strategy, mode layouts, bank-placement inference
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: serial-shift strategy (5 sequential writes deliver one bit each; bit-7 write resets the sequence) as an instruction-sequence state machine over the dataflow engine; mode-register strategy for MMC1 control (PRG modes: 32K / fix-first / fix-last); mode-dependent layouts from schema v2. Flagship for BANK-PLACEMENT INFERENCE: MMC1's 16K banks fit either $8000 or $C000 — assign windows by following flows (recovered switch values, self-reference consistency of each bank's absolute refs, vector anchors) with provenance recorded and user override available; no upfront per-bank options (retires the GhidraNes BankAddressOption pattern, BankAddressOption.java:13-80). Acceptance targets: Metroid, Zelda, Final Fantasy (also a GME AKAO-adjacent interest).
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, NESdev wiki cross-checked live). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-6a7 (layouts runtime) filed separately.

MMC1 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: any $8000-$FFFF write with bit 7 set clears the shifter AND ORs Control with $0C (prg_mode -> 3, mirroring untouched) — unconditional. Commit = 5 bit-7-clear writes, bit 0 each; address bits 14:13 matter ONLY on write 5 (00=Control, 01=CHR0, 10=CHR1, 11=PRG bank). Consecutive-cycle ignore: emulation-only, do not model. Control: bits 0-1 mirroring, 2-3 prg_mode (0/1=32K, 2=fix-first, 3=fix-last; 3 = reset-dance default), bit 4 CHR (defer). EMPIRICAL KEY: real games do the reset dance once, early, and never write Control again -> prg_mode is fully known (=3) nearly everywhere; placement "inference" is a rare-residual problem, not the main path.

DESIGN A — serial-shift (the crux):
- Bit-7 reset: ordinary single-write computeSwitch (recognize known bit-7 via existing backward scan; emit prg_mode=3 known, mirroring knownness pass-through). NO engine change.
- Fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR: five DISTINCT static instructions; strategy statically walks the chain, returns null for writes 1-4, full BankState at write 5 (target from ITS address bits 14:13, value reassembled from the chain). NO engine change.
- CANONICAL LOOP (STA/LSR/DEY/BNE, inlined or JSR'd) — REJECTED APPROACH: shift-register position as hidden BankState fields fails PROVABLY: the loop-head join merges position 0 (entry) with 1-4 (back-edge) -> per-bit AND-agree makes position permanently unknown on the FIRST merge (monotone-shrinking within a pass) -> honest strategy must poison every commit -> 100% of the majority idiom unresolvable. Loop unrolling also rejected (p-code trace replay = emulator territory; listing-level duplication fights Ghidra).
- WORKABLE: idiom recognition, extending the findHelpers precedent one level down. New optional hook on BankSwitchStrategy — findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty — run per function like findHelpers; BoardBankAnalyzer folds matches into the same switchResults-shaped map, so merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation need NO further changes (the load-bearing containment property). Recognize: STA-to-range as sole loop-body write + shift of same reg + counted dec-branch trip=5 (or 4+preloop); seed value resolved by the existing scanner applied ONCE to the pre-loop load; commit attached to the loop's EXIT edge (STA's own outState stays no-change).
- Honest degrade: table-driven/memory-seeded values -> existing WARNING path. CHR0/CHR1 targets: structurally recognized, zero tracked fields (verify "recognized but discarded" with a fixture).

DESIGN B — mode handling: MMC1 DOES NOT instantiate a mode-register mechanism — mirroring/prg_mode arrive inside the serial Control byte. serial-shift params need multi-field-per-target deposit:
  targets: {0: {fields: [{name: mirroring, shift: 0, bits: 2}, {name: prg_mode, shift: 2, bits: 2}]}, 3: {fields: [{name: prg_bank, shift: 0, bits: 5}]}}  # 1,2 (CHR) omitted
Params are strategy-opaque pass-through in MapCompiler — no compiler change. Layouts schema (memory.layouts[]/when:) is ALREADY compiled+validated; the gap is runtime consumption (shared bead). MMC1-specific layout wrinkle: 32K mode (0/1) is a genuinely DIFFERENT window (PRG32_B<v>, bank LSB ignored), not a merge of the two 16K windows; confirm during the shared bead that this needs no third window-shape concept. Naming: keep WINDOW_B<v> when shape doesn't vary by mode; WINDOW_M<mode>_B<v> only when it does.

DESIGN C — placement inference, two tiers:
- Tier 1 (primary, retires GhidraNes BankAddressOption by construction): loader materializes the (layout x bank) cross product (MMC1 acceptance titles are 128K = 8 banks; mode 2/3 has ONE switchable 16K window -> real count ~banks x 2, inside the tolerable ceiling); analyzer retargeting does the two-level (mode -> window-set -> bank) lookup from TRACKED state. No upfront user options; normal dataflow resolves placement.
- Tier 2 (rare residual, mode/bank partially unknown): (b) self-reference consistency scoring (candidate bank's absolute refs in-range at $8000 vs $C000; raw-byte operand-pattern scan as a pre-disassembly signal only); (c) vector/fixed-window anchors (last/second_last image offsets, like labelVectorTargets); unresolvable -> existing WARNING, never guess.
- Provenance: extend annotateBankSwitch EOL text with evidence tier ("[switch-value flow]" vs "[inferred: self-ref 7/8]"). Override: loader Option string ("bank=N:window" pairs) via PROGRAM_INFO options, matching BOARD_OPTION_NAME precedent. Analyzer-time overlay-block CREATION (for over-budget boards): legal per Memory API but unproven here (analyzer has no FileBytes; byte-array overload via Memory.getBytes) — DEFERRED from M3 explicitly.

SUB-BEADS (proposed order 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5; 2 can parallel 1):
1. layouts runtime [SHARED with grm-6a7 — filed as its own bead; MEDIUM-HIGH risk; existing goldens must not regress]
2. mode-register strategy class [LOW; MMC3 needs it, MMC1 doesn't; register-write-shaped]
3. serial-shift strategy [HIGH — the findIdioms hook is new engine surface; fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable, CHR-write-discarded; build loop matcher from REAL commercial MMC1 disassembly patterns, not wiki-invented shapes]
4. nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring (ines_mappers: [1]) [LOW-MED; where the seams meet; end-to-end Metroid-shaped fixture]
5. placement Tier 2 + provenance/override [MED; not required for acceptance-title correctness]
+ manual acceptance gate: Metroid/Zelda/FF1 (real ROMs, CI-excluded per convention).

RISKS: findIdioms hook shape unproven — prototype against landed layouts plumbing BEFORE committing to the descriptor (a hook that doesn't fold into switchResults ripples back); loop-matcher brittleness (DEX vs DEY, 4+1 shapes) — source patterns from real disassemblies; bit-7 partially-known must not silently assume reset (explicit fixture); 32K-window identity question (above).
notes: Design attached 2026-07-10 (research: serial-shift loop idiom requires a findIdioms engine hook — lattice-position-field approach provably fails at the loop-head join; MMC1 needs NO mode-register mechanism, mode bits arrive in the serial Control byte; placement inference demoted to rare-residual Tier 2 since real games fix prg_mode=3 once). Shared layouts-runtime prerequisite = grm-5tl.18. Proposed sub-bead split in design; materialize as children when work starts. Prototype the findIdioms hook shape against landed grm-5tl.18 plumbing BEFORE writing the descriptor.

title: BankingAnalyzer: resolve masked RMW bank switches (LDA $01 / AND #imm / ORA #imm / STA $01)
description: Optional improvement (user request, 2026-07-05). The backward scan in C64BankingAnalyzer.resolveStoredImmediate only recognizes a direct immediate load (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm), so the frequent bit-preserving switch idiom — LDA $01; AND #$F8; ORA #$05; STA $01 (preserving cassette bits 3-5) — currently degrades to UNKNOWN + warning bookmark. Two implementation routes: (a) extend the backward scan to evaluate AND/ORA immediate chains symbolically over just the bank bits: after AND #imm the tracked bits are prev&imm, after ORA #imm prev|imm; whenever (andImm & mechanism.mask)==0 the ORA fully determines the new state (state = oraImm & mask) with NO knowledge of the prior value — this covers the canonical idiom statically; chains that leave bank bits dependent on the unknown prior value stay UNKNOWN. (b) heavier: use SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext to ask for the register value at the store (handles loads from other addresses, TAX chains etc.) — more coverage, more machinery. Route (a) recommended first; keep (b) as a follow-on if real PRGs show patterns (a) misses. Gotcha reminder: bare immediates come from getOpObjects() Scalar, not CodeUnit.getScalar().
notes:
ORDERING REVISED (user, 2026-07-05): PREFER existing Ghidra register-value-tracking infrastructure over the custom backward scan — try route (b) FIRST: SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext (ghidra.program.util; the engine behind ConstantPropagationAnalyzer, confirmed in the gib.2 hook-point research to track register->value/space along flow) to ask for the stored register's value at the STA $01 site; also check whether ProgramContext already holds an analysis-set value there. If the infra route is impractical for our analyzer's position in the pipeline (e.g. constant propagation hasn't run yet at REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), or 6502 coverage is weak), THEN fall back to route (a): extend the backward scan with the AND/ORA mask algebra (bits = (prev & andImm) | oraImm; known iff andImm clears all mechanism.mask bits). Scan route stays documented as the fallback, not the default.
DESIGN (2026-07-07, pre-dispatch): mask-algebra backward scan formalized — maintain (A_acc,O_acc) meaning final=(x&A_acc)|O_acc over unknown prior x; seed A_acc=0xFF,O_acc=0 at the store; stepping BACK over AND #a: A_acc'=a&A_acc; over ORA #o: O_acc'=(o&A_acc)|O_acc; bank bit determined iff A_acc bit==0 or O_acc bit==1; early-stop when all mechanism.mask bits determined (prior register content irrelevant); LDA #imm terminates fully-known with state=((imm&A_acc)|O_acc)&mask. Subsumes the existing immediate-load case. EOR/RMW-in-place stay UNKNOWN. INFRA EXPECTATION to verify: SymbolicPropogator tracks full values, so LDA $01 (memory read) poisons the chain — likely CANNOT resolve the masked idiom; subagent must time-box the infra investigation, report the conclusion, and implement the algebra as the core resolver either way (infra consult optional if trivially feasible).
DESIGN REFINEMENT (user, 2026-07-07): track PORT BITS individually, not just the combined PLA state — LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 (BASIC off via LORAM bit 0) leaves bit0 KNOWN=0 with bits1-2 unknown; per-bit knowledge still determines windows whose occupant agrees across all consistent states. Representation: PortState(knownMask,bits); dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits (knownMask' = k1&k2&~(v1^v2)). KEY COMPOSITION WIN: when the chain's base load is LDA $01 itself, x = the tracked in-state at the store — so masked RMW from a fully-known state resolves EXACTLY (7 -> AND #$FE -> 6), no heuristic. Bit known iff aAcc bit==0 (forced 0) | oAcc bit==1 (forced 1) | (base==port-load AND in-state bit known). FALLBACK (user): for still-unknown bits, assume initial_state values when resolving occupants; bank comments must distinguish known vs assumed bits; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known at a mechanism store. Abort composition if backward scan crosses another mechanism write.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2 headless, banktest2 + banktest regression). Per-bit PortState(knownMask,bits) replaces the int state: dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits only (monotone shrink, terminating); store resolution = backward mask-algebra scan with (aAcc,oAcc) accumulators composing AND#imm/ORA#imm, terminating at LDA#imm (fully known), a load of the mechanism address itself (base = tracked in-state — so LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 from known state 5 resolves EXACTLY to 4), or any clobber incl. crossing calls (review fix: JSR fall-through passes the block-linkage check, so calls must clobber explicitly) and crossing mechanism writes (abort, unsound to inherit). Occupant resolution assumes initial_state for unknown bits (user fallback); partial switches get 'bank -> 7? (...) [known: LORAM=1; assumed from initial: HIRAM,CHAREN]' comments; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known. INFRA FINDING (step 0): SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext track whole register values — LDA $01 (unknown memory) poisons the chain; no per-bit partial-knowledge model exists in-tree, so the mask algebra is necessary, not a workaround. All 6 banktest2 criteria + 4 banktest regression criteria pass.

title: Descriptor schema: per-occupant executable override (CHARGEN font ROM should be x=false)
description: canExecute() in C64PrgLoader derives the execute permission purely from kind (rom->x=true), so the CHARGEN overlay is currently marked executable even though it is glyph bitmap data. Add an optional per-occupant/per-region 'executable:' override to the YAML schema + map compiler + loader (default stays kind-derived), and set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Surfaced by the gib.2 RFC execute-mode discussion (2026-07-05): the RFC's analyzer-compat example claims a sensible descriptor marks font ROM non-executable — make our own descriptor do so.
design: DECISION (user, 2026-07-05): Option 1 — kind-derived defaults + sparse per-attribute overrides. Optional boolean fields readable:/writable:/executable: allowed anywhere a kind appears (region, occupant, subregion); kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w (non-x). Rationale/rule for future cases: one-attribute deviation => override; multi-behavior cluster (perms+structs+volatility+storage like io) => new kind. Rejected: new kinds per combo (code change per quirk, taxonomy explosion — option-3-with-worse-ergonomics), required direct perms (abstraction inversion: descriptor states what hardware IS, tools derive treatment; boilerplate; allows kind-contradicting perms). Precedent: MAME address maps (.rom()/.ram() + per-range modifiers). Riders: (a) document kind->defaults table in SCHEMA.md (currently implicit in loader canWrite/canExecute); (b) derive volatile=true for io-kind blocks in loader (MemoryBlock.setVolatile) — stops decompiler folding repeated $D012 reads; (c) set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Verify: rebuild + headless smoke shows CHARGEN x=false and IO blocks volatile.
close_reason: Implemented + headless-verified. Sparse readable/writable/executable overrides (kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w) at region/occupant/subregion level across MapCompiler passthrough + loader Perms record/perms() helper; io-kind blocks now marked volatile (setVolatile). c64.yaml: CHARGEN executable:false (headline) + COLOR_RAM executable:false (review catch — kind:ram default would have flipped it x=true vs baseline; 4-bit cells, open-bus fetches; first organic use of the new override). SCHEMA.md gained the kind->defaults table + one-attribute-deviation=>override / multi-behavior-cluster=>new-kind rule; MAP_FORMAT.md documents the passthrough fields. Smoke: CHARGEN x=false, COLOR_RAM x=false vol=false, VIC/SID/CIA/P6510/IO1/IO2 vol=true, baseline otherwise unchanged, Import succeeded.

title: Generalized string detection: PETSCII + per-game tile-table text mappings
description:
Future feature: extend string detection beyond ASCII for retro systems.
- C64: PETSCII (KERNAL/CHROUT strings) AND screen codes (direct screen-RAM writes) — two DIFFERENT mappings, each with shifted/unshifted charset variants. Prior art: PETSCII visualizer in grue74/ghidra-c64helpers fork (inspect for reuse ideas).
- NES/SNES: per-game tile->character mappings, published as .tbl 'table files' by the ROM-hacking/translation community (romhacking.net, Data Crystal) — a de-facto standard format we could ingest directly, giving per-game string detection from community-documented data.
Integration points to investigate: Ghidra string data types support pluggable Java Charsets (extension could register PETSCII charsets); string-search analyzer charset hooks; descriptor schema could reference charset/table per system or per game.
Fits the descriptor-driven vision: text encoding is system knowledge (or game knowledge, for tile tables) that belongs in data, not code.
notes: DESIGN INPUT (user, 2026-07-11): the CBM BASIC detokenizing analyzer (grm-odt.1, epic grm-1.6) now DEPENDS ON this bead and is its first concrete consumer — its needs must inform this design, not be retrofitted. Requirements from that consumer: (1) a Java-callable byte->display-string mapping API for PETSCII usable OUTSIDE Ghidra's charset/string-search machinery — the detokenizer builds EOL comment text programmatically (string literals inside quotes, raw REM text) and cannot go through StringDataInstance; (2) both PETSCII variants (shifted/unshifted) selectable per call site; screen codes are a SEPARATE mapping (direct screen-RAM writes) the detokenizer does NOT need — do not conflate; (3) control/graphics bytes ($00-$1F, $80-$FF inside quotes) need a printable escaped rendering convention (e.g. {CLR}, {RVS ON}, {c-A}) — pick one, document it, and keep it stable since it lands in golden test dumps; (4) the mapping data should be data-driven (descriptor/shared data file) per project convention, and shared with any future Ghidra charset registration rather than duplicated. Suggested shape: a small PetsciiMapper (or CharsetTable) class + data file, with Ghidra Charset registration layered on top later for string search. The NES/SNES .tbl half of this bead is unaffected by the BASIC consumer but should share the table-data plumbing where natural.

title: NES board descriptors: Bandai FCG family (mappers 16/157/159) + GxROM (mapper 66)
description: Board-coverage work: Bandai FCG family + GxROM descriptors, using the Dragon Ball ROM collection at Z:/nes/db as real-ROM TEST CASES (user, 2026-07-12: the DB games are NOT music-extraction targets themselves -- they are convenient exercisers for these mappers). Mapper census from Z:/nes/db/mappers.txt: 6x mapper 016 (Bandai FCG/LZ93D50), 2x mapper 066 (GXROM), 1x 157 (Datach Joint ROM System), 1x 159 (LZ93D50 + 24C01 EEPROM). GxROM is the easy half: one register at $8000-$FFFF, PRG bits 4-5 select a 32K bank, CHR bits 0-1 -- a single memory-latch mechanism, simpler than the shipped UxROM board. Bandai FCG is a register-file board: registers at $6000-$7FFF and/or $8000-$FFFF (submapper-dependent), $8/$8008 = 16K PRG bank at $8000 (fixed last bank at $C000), regs 0-7 = CHR banks, $A = IRQ control -- shaped like a select-less multi-register variant; likely fits existing register-write strategy with one mechanism per register address, or motivates a small 'register-file' generalization. 157/159 differ mainly in EEPROM wiring (irrelevant to PRG banking) -- one descriptor with ines_mappers [16,159] plus a Datach variant may suffice; verify against FCEU source at Z:/nes/fceu/boards/bandai.c (local reference implementation) and NESdev. Fixture-first per the banktest discipline; real-ROM check against the Z:/nes/db set.
notes: Z:/nes also holds the FCEU emulator source tree (Z:/nes/fceu, boards/ dir = C reference implementations for every mapper) -- useful oracle for ALL future NES board descriptors, not just these.

title: SMC: decrypt-on-the-fly — EOR-decryptor recognition and emulation-assisted image recovery
description: Use case 2: C64 copy-protection-era code stored encrypted and EORed (with itself, a constant, or a rolling key) in place at runtime, then executed. Static listing of the encrypted bytes is garbage; naive disassembly poisons analysis. Approach candidates (evaluate in this order): (a) EMULATION-ASSISTED: recognize the decryptor entry (small, self-contained loop), run it in Ghidra's p-code emulator (Debugger machinery, headless-scriptable) over a snapshot, capture the decrypted range, and write it back as an alternate view (overlay block 'DECRYPTED_xxxx' or patched bytes + provenance bookmark) for static analysis to proceed; (b) STATIC pattern-match of the common EOR-self/EOR-constant loops (feasible for the simple constant case, hopeless for chained/rolling schemes); (c) documented manual workflow (emulator memory dump import). In-place decryption also needs a 'these bytes were replaced' provenance model — decide whether original-encrypted vs decrypted views both stay navigable. Research Ghidra Debugger emulator APIs for headless use as part of this bead; findings feed the epic's static-vs-emulation design tension.
notes: 2026-07-13 TIER 2 NOW VERIFIED (grm-yxn closed). Both emulation outcomes tested: rolling key (initialized RAM) -> trusted NOTE overlay; hardware key (CIA $DC00) -> suspect WARNING overlay. Tiers 1 (constant, inline) and 2 (rolling/computed, emulated) are both implemented AND tested end-to-end through the real import pipeline (commits 2d3815f, 58d3c03, 2aa079b). REMAINING (minor polish, not blocking): (1) tier-3 'refer to manual workflow' -- the suspect WARNING is the 'detect+downgrade' half; adding VICE-snapshot/Debugger referral TEXT to the warning message is trivial follow-up; (2) auto-disassemble the DECRYPTED_xxxx overlay so the recovered payload shows as code (currently bytes only); (3) generalize beyond C64PrgLoader gate if a second platform needs it. Core deliverable (EOR-decryptor recognition + emulation-assisted image recovery) is DONE and tested.
close_reason: Decrypt-on-the-fly SMC recovery complete and tested end-to-end via the banktest suite. C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer recognizes the in-place EOR decrypt loop and recovers the plaintext into a DECRYPTED_xxxx overlay (encrypted original stays navigable), disassembled as code, with provenance bookmarks + cross-link comment. TIER 1 (constant EOR): inline byte XOR (fixture decryptloop). TIER 2 (rolling/computed): routed to the grm-edg EmulationRecovery harness, run in the p-code emulator during analysis, read back under a dirty-watch -- verified for both the trusted outcome (rolling key in RAM -> NOTE, fixture rollingdecrypt) and the hardware-tainted outcome (CIA-register key -> provenance suspect -> WARNING + manual-recovery referral text, fixture suspectdecrypt). TIER 3 (hardware-keyed): detect-and-refer implemented (WARNING bookmark points at VICE .vsf snapshot import / Debugger Copy-Into-Program). Safety: only the clean down-counting LDX/DEX/BPL form with a JMP into range is auto-applied; everything else is a candidate/warning, never rewritten. No false positives (dump() bookmark filter is *BankingAnalyzer-scoped; no existing golden changed). Key impl note: an indexed operand's base is a Scalar not an Address (no static ref for base+index), so indexedBase accepts both. Commits 2d3815f (tier1), 58d3c03+2aa079b (tier2 via grm-yxn), 8da7796 (polish). REMAINING (deferred, non-blocking): generalize beyond the C64PrgLoader gate to a 6502-generic analyzer if a second platform needs it -- YAGNI until then.
